external_research.body_md:
## Volatility-regime conditioning and factor crowding are the dominant 2026 themes for mid-frequency equity quants; residual-decomposition and factor-timing upgrades offer directly actionable improvements to existing momentum and sector-rotation strategies.

### Volatility-Conditional Momentum: VIX Spikes Are the Primary Culprit

Haim Mozes ('Volatility Spikes and Momentum', Journal of Beta Investment Strategies, Spring 2026) documents that VIX spikes (defined as VIX ≥ 1.5× its 3-month MA) occurred 22 times in 2014-2024 vs only 7 times in 2004-2013. Momentum returns averaged -0.73%/month in spike months and the immediately following month, vs +0.54%/month otherwise; over the full 2014-2024 period, momentum averaged only 2.23% annualised — explaining the decade-long underperformance. The mechanism is that spike-driven reversals catch momentum portfolios positioned for continuation.

**Implication:** fits existing: momentum-trader — add a VIX-state gate (reduce gross exposure or pause new entries when VIX > 1.5× its 60-day MA; resume only after one calm month confirms the spike has passed)

### Factor Crowding: Anomaly-Driven Demand Is Now Self-Referential

Posselt & Kjær ('Anomaly-Driven Demand', March 2026), covered by Larry Swedroe for Alpha Architect (May 22, 2026), demonstrate that factor rebalancing by the collective strategy cohort is large enough to mechanically move prices, particularly at month-start and in stocks sitting at the intersection of multiple anomaly portfolios simultaneously. A measurable fraction of observed factor alpha is generated by the coordinated buying of other factor investors, not underlying economic fundamentals — making it fragile to cohort shrinkage. Widely-followed screens (price momentum, low-vol, value overlap) are most affected.

**Implication:** spawn-candidate: a calendar-aware momentum variant that rebalances mid-month (e.g. 10th trading day) rather than end-of-month to avoid buying into the crowded demand pulse and selling into the unwind

### Dynamic Factor Timing via Factor Momentum: Validated on ETFs

Tai, Leung & Jimenez (SSRN 6224058, February 12, 2026) show that rotating between factor ETFs (value/momentum/quality/low-vol) using a simple factor-momentum signal — the same factor that outperformed recently continues to outperform — achieves a Sharpe of 0.66 vs 0.59 for equal-weight, 13.0% vs 11.3% annualised, with a 78.6% calendar-year hit rate over 1998-2025. Turnover is ~3× annually. Crucially, the authors validate the strategy on actual ETF prices and find only modest degradation from tracking error and expense ratios, confirming retail implementability.

**Implication:** fits existing: sector-rotator — upgrade the scoring function from raw sector ETF relative-strength to a factor-momentum-weighted composite, i.e. rank sector ETFs by the momentum of their recent momentum score rather than the score itself

### Residual vs Systematic Return Decomposition in Industry Momentum

Gao, Li, Yuan & Zhou (SSRN 6371558, March 8, 2026) decompose short-term returns into idiosyncratic and systematic components and find that while individual stocks exhibit 1-month reversal, industry, characteristic, and factor portfolios exhibit short-term momentum. A 'residual-to-systematic reversal' component is embedded within raw industry momentum, partially cancelling the signal and causing standard spanning regressions to misattribute its source. Hedging out this residual component substantially strengthens industry momentum profits and demonstrates that industry momentum is economically distinct from — and additive to — factor momentum.

**Implication:** fits existing: sector-rotator — when scoring sectors, subtract the cross-sectional stock-level reversal component (i.e. don't let a sector score be dragged down by its own internal short-term reversals); practically, score sectors using a cap-weighted-smoothed return rather than the simple average return across member stocks

### ESG Ratings as State-Dependent Drawdown Insurance

Yi, Hu, Sun & Chen (arXiv 2605.04479, May 6, 2026; NTU / Cornell / JHU / UT Austin) use Double Machine Learning to deconfound selection bias and show that high-ESG portfolios materially reduce discrete crash incidence during systemic drawdowns. Protection is concentrated at adverse quantiles only — not a full-distribution shift — and comes with a measurable performance drag in stable regimes. This is the first paper to identify ESG protection as *priced* insurance (the drag is the premium) rather than free alpha, which changes the framing from 'ESG factor' to 'drawdown hedge'.

**Implication:** fits existing: macro-aligned — use an ESG quality tier (e.g. MSCI ESG rating ≥ AA) as an additional stock-universe filter that activates only in stressed regimes (yield-curve inversion or DXY risk-off), trading some upside for a lower crash-incidence profile

### Sources

- https://ibkrcampus.com/campus/ibkr-quant-news/why-momentum-investing-has-been-struggling-and-what-volatility-has-to-do-with-it/
- https://alphaarchitect.com/momentum-investing-struggling/
- https://larryswedroe.substack.com/p/when-everyone-trades-the-same-factor
- https://alphaarchitect.com/factor-strategies/
- https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6224058
- https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=6371558
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04479

LLM-driven. Trades bond ETFs based on yield-curve shape, central-bank
stance, and credit spreads. US: TLT/IEF/SHY/HYG/LQD. UK/EU: Gilts +
Bunds + EUR credit ETFs. Same strategy bias, different bond universe
per region.

executed.thesis: The 5.28x volume spike on Friday signals institutional accumulation ahead of Monday's open; falling 10Y yields (-10bp week-over-week to 4.453%) driven by oil's collapse from the stagflationary regime provide the macro catalyst for this global govt bond ETF to extend its +1.36% 5d move.
executed.outcome_notes: Price returned exactly to entry at the scheduled exit — no directional move was captured within the holding window. The volume spike on Friday did not translate into follow-through buying at Monday's open, suggesting the institutional accumulation signal was either noise or already exhausted before entry. The yield-decline macro catalyst apparently stalled or was already priced in.
executed.risks_observed: All three basket legs were duration-long bond instruments, so a pause or reversal in the yield move hit all simultaneously — concentration in a single macro factor with no diversifying offset. Scheduled exits remove the ability to ride a delayed thesis, turning a timing miss into a guaranteed friction loss.

executed.thesis: IG credit is the cleanest expression of the current quality bid — LQD outperformed HYG by 59bp last week and ISXF.L's MACD hist at +0.258 is the strongest credit momentum signal in the candidate set, confirmed by the +0.73% return from the prior hold.
executed.outcome_notes: IG credit produced no price follow-through from the MACD momentum signal within the holding period. Given the prior hold already returned +0.73%, the momentum may have been a lagging confirmation of a move that was largely complete at entry rather than a leading signal.
executed.risks_observed: MACD hist at a cycle high is a coincident indicator on a short hold — if the credit spread tightening was already done, entry was chasing. The basket ran three correlated fixed-income longs with identical scheduled exits, meaning a single stalled macro environment (yields flat, spreads stable) wiped friction costs across all legs at once.

executed.thesis: 15-year gilts offer direct duration exposure to falling UK long yields; RSI at 58.8 is the least-extended among the gilt candidates and adequate volume (1.27x) provides cleaner execution than thinner alternatives like GLTL.L (0.11x).
executed.outcome_notes: The 15Y gilt position moved nowhere by the scheduled exit, despite the yield-decline setup. RSI headroom and adequate volume gave clean execution but provided no edge on direction; the underlying gilt yield apparently did not fall materially during the holding window.
executed.risks_observed: Gilt-specific drivers — UK fiscal headlines, BoE rate path divergence from global peers — were absent from the selection criteria, leaving unpriced idiosyncratic risk in what was framed as a pure duration trade. Scheduled exit with no trailing stop meant there was no mechanism to capture even a small intraday move if it occurred outside the exit window.

executed.thesis: 3x leveraged gilt long is the cleanest expression of the ongoing yield-relief theme — 10Y down 6bp and 30Y down 8bp WoW — and only requires gilts to ease another 3-4bp to clear the 1% cost gate; MACD histogram at +0.695 (highest in group), RSI 59 (room to run), and above both MAs confirm the short-term momentum is intact.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was unchanged at exit — the incremental 3–4bp yield easing needed to cover costs never materialised during the holding window, leaving the position flat on price and the entire P&L loss attributable to spread/transaction friction. The scheduled exit triggered with momentum signals still nominally intact, so the trade was a timing miss rather than a thesis failure per se.

active.description:
LLM-driven. Trades commodity ETFs based on dollar index, real yields,
supply/demand themes. Commodities are dollar-denominated globally so the
same US-listed ETF universe (GLD, SLV, USO, DBA, DBB) is used in both
regions — only the underlying decision logic differs by macro regime.

executed.thesis: Natural gas is running an independent uptrend (+12.91% 20d, UNG +12.55% 20d) entirely decoupled from oil's collapse — this is the one commodity with a clean supply/demand momentum story today. Volume at 1.63x confirms active participation, MACD histogram positive, above both SMAs; using the unleveraged 1x instrument avoids the stop-hunt risk that ended 3UNG.L last Thursday.
executed.outcome_notes: Price went nowhere intraday — entry and exit were identical, so the natural gas momentum thesis had no opportunity to express itself within the holding window. The scheduled exit captured only friction costs, suggesting the catalyst needed more time to develop or the session lacked follow-through participation despite the prior multi-day trend.
executed.risks_observed: A flat exit on a momentum name reveals that volume confirmation at entry does not guarantee intraday continuation — the 1.63x volume signal may have reflected prior-session activity rather than fresh buying pressure. Holding through a scheduled exit without a trailing stop means there was no mechanism to protect against an intraday reversal that happened to close flat.

executed.thesis: Silver gets dual tailwinds today: dollar grinding lower (DXY -0.39% 5d) is a direct USD-denominated commodity boost, and the growth revival regime drives industrial silver demand. The 2.73x volume ratio is the strongest demand signal in the entire candidate list — real institutional buying is occurring — and RSI at 65 is elevated but not at an extreme that would suggest exhaustion.
executed.outcome_notes: Silver likewise printed no movement between entry and scheduled exit, so neither the dollar tailwind nor the industrial-demand thesis was validated or refuted on this session. The strongest volume signal in the candidate list did not translate into price displacement, which warrants checking whether the volume ratio was front-loaded in the pre-market or early session.
executed.risks_observed: Silver, copper, and natural gas were all held simultaneously — if a risk-off macro shock had hit intraday, all three would have moved together and amplified drawdown despite appearing to be diversified across commodities. The basket also shares a common dependency on DXY direction, making it effectively a leveraged dollar-weakness bet with commodity-sector labelling obscuring the correlation.

executed.thesis: Copper macro remains the cleanest structural story: EV/grid buildout demand, dollar weakness amplifying USD-priced commodity returns, and global growth revival confirmed by the W23 macro view. COPG.L has the best volume (0.85x) and MACD in the copper cluster, and my recent COPP.L +3.38% confirms the thesis is still live — choosing COPG.L over COPP.L for better liquidity.
executed.outcome_notes: COPG.L held flat from entry to scheduled exit, contributing nothing beyond friction loss. The structural copper thesis (EV/grid demand, dollar weakness) is multi-week in nature and did not produce intraday price action; the positive COPP.L reference trade was prior-session evidence, not a same-day signal.
executed.risks_observed: All three basket positions exited at exactly their entry prices, suggesting either very wide spreads being disguised as zero movement or a genuinely directionless session — either scenario should prompt a review of whether scheduled exits are the right exit mechanic for a momentum strategy where the edge requires price to move before costs are recovered. The repeated occurrence across all three names points to a systemic issue rather than single-stock idiosyncrasy.

executed.thesis: Copper in a clean uptrend — above SMA20 and SMA50, MACD positive, consistent +8% across both 5d and 20d timeframes. Dollar stalling below 99 and DBB base metals +5.64% 20d provide the macro tailwind; volume at 0.78x average is normal for this product.
executed.outcome_notes: Price advanced steadily to the scheduled exit without requiring active management, confirming the uptrend thesis held throughout the hold period. The dollar remaining soft and base metals sector momentum sustaining the bid were the clear drivers; no adverse intraday reversal tested the position.
executed.risks_observed: COPP.L exposure runs correlated with any other base metals positions in the basket, so a sharp dollar reversal would have hit multiple legs simultaneously. Volume at 0.78x is thin enough that spread friction on entry and exit meaningfully erodes realised return on a move of this size.

executed.thesis: Above both SMAs with RSI 66 and positive MACD, but the key signal is today's 2.47x volume surge alongside +15.38% 20d momentum — elevated conviction from clear institutional flow. The cross-asset setup (dollar stalling, macro transitional) supports continuation.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was flat at the scheduled exit, meaning transaction costs (spread, commission, FX conversion) produced the net loss on a zero-move position. The 2.47x volume surge on entry day did not sustain into directional price action, suggesting the flow was a single-session event — possibly distribution — rather than the start of accumulation.
executed.risks_observed: Using an isolated volume spike as the primary conviction signal carries an inherent false-signal risk: elevated volume without price follow-through is a recognised distribution pattern. With no price move to absorb costs, the entire P&L was friction drag, which points to a minimum-expected-move threshold being missing from the entry filter for low-priced, lightly traded instruments.

executed.thesis: Natural gas in a strong uptrend — UNG +17.14% 20d and +3.48% 5d, 3UNG above SMA20 with MACD histogram turning positive. Sized small (20%) to account for today's thin volume (0.13 ratio) and 3x leverage requiring a wider stop; wider TP reflects the levered upside.
executed.outcome_notes: The stop was triggered on an intraday reversal, with the 3x leverage amplifying a moderate natural gas pullback into the full -5% loss. Entry into a 0.13x volume day created wide-spread conditions from the start, meaning the effective entry was worse than the mid-price and the stop distance was narrower in real terms than the nominal level implied.
executed.risks_observed: A 3x leveraged ETP with sub-0.15x average daily volume is structurally prone to stop-hunting: thin books mean small order flow can push price through stops, and the leverage ratio amplifies every tick against the position. The 20% position sizing limited absolute damage, but if any other energy or risk-on leg was live concurrently, a gas reversal driven by macro news would correlate across the basket simultaneously.

executed.thesis: DBB is the only commodity ETF above both its 20d and 50d SMA with RSI momentum still above 60; the dollar's failure to break 100 eliminates the primary cross-asset headwind, and the macro view's residual growth optimism (DBB +3.46% 20d) supports the copper/aluminum complex. Capped at a single-day hold given low volume conditions on 2026-05-26 — no reason to extend exposure into a potentially thin market.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the hold period and exited at the scheduled end-of-day without touching any active stop, suggesting the momentum signal stalled rather than reversed sharply. The base metals complex did not follow through on the residual growth optimism; the dollar's stability at the 100 level removed the tailwind rather than providing one, and DBB gave back ground steadily rather than in a single flush.
executed.risks_observed: Single-name commodity ETF with no intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed passively — a trailing stop at entry or a modest intraday exit trigger would have reduced the loss. The one-day hold discipline was correctly applied given thin volume, but the position still carried full notional exposure into a session where the underlying metals complex lacked a catalyst, making the risk/reward asymmetric from the open.

executed.thesis: Dollar at 99.07 and trending slightly weaker provides a USD-priced commodity tailwind; DBB is the only candidate above SMA20 with RSI 61 confirming healthy uptrend momentum and no overbought risk. Base metals structural demand from EV/grid capex supports the bid; MACD deceleration is negligible at -0.011.
executed.outcome_notes: Price went nowhere — the scheduled exit captured zero movement, suggesting the momentum impulse simply didn't fire within the holding window. The USD tailwind and RSI conditions held as backdrop but generated no follow-through; the sterling loss reflects FX drag or transaction costs on a flat price, not adverse price action.
executed.risks_observed: Single-name basket means the full book was riding one instrument with no cross-asset offset — any surprise China PMI print or LME inventory release could have moved this sharply with nothing to absorb it. Scheduled exit is a blunt instrument here: no mechanism to distinguish 'thesis is early' from 'thesis is wrong', so valid setups get cut the same as failed ones, eroding edge on momentum strategies that need time to develop.

executed.thesis: DBB is the only commodity ETF with intact technical structure today — above both SMAs, RSI 60.7, volume slightly above average — while the Iran deal removes the oil-geopolitical premium that crowded out base metals. Dollar softness is a marginal tailwind for copper/aluminum/zinc priced in USD.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted modestly higher from entry to exit, consistent with a soft-dollar, base-metals-positive backdrop, but the move was minimal — the Iran deal catalyst and dollar weakness didn't produce meaningful intraday momentum. Exit was scheduled rather than driven by a target hit, suggesting the thesis was directionally correct but lacked the velocity to generate alpha.
executed.risks_observed: Single-position basket means all risk sat in one ETF with no offsetting legs; if base metals had reversed on renewed dollar strength or a surprise inventory build, there was no hedge. The thesis depended on two macro factors (Iran deal follow-through and dollar softness) that could both fade quickly, and neither had been confirmed as sustained at entry.

executed.thesis: Iran war premium is firmly embedded — no diplomatic progress (talks stalled, US seized an Iranian tanker intraday) and a 9.1M barrel API crude draw against a 3.4M est confirms physical tightness on both the geopolitical and fundamental axes. Technicals support continuation: RSI 64.8, MACD positive, price 8.4% above SMA20; 1-day hold keeps the position clear of overnight diplomatic headline risk.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved against the position immediately and hit the stop, suggesting the geopolitical premium was already priced in at entry or unwound intraday — the API draw failed to sustain the bid. The thesis required continued momentum; instead the market faded, likely on profit-taking or a softening of the Iran headline after the tanker seizure was digested.
executed.risks_observed: The entry was chasing an already-extended move (8.4% above SMA20, RSI near overbought territory), leaving little cushion if sentiment reversed on any diplomatic noise or a weaker-than-expected prompt spread. Geopolitical premium trades carry binary headline risk that a 1-day hold does not fully avoid — a partial de-escalation signal intraday was sufficient to collapse the thesis before the stop could be managed.

executed.thesis: Oil supply shock thesis is intact — Iran military standoff maintains a risk premium regardless of Monday's tactical delay, and USO's technicals confirm active momentum (above SMA20/50, RSI 62, +23% 20d). Wider stop accommodates intraday diplomatic headline volatility without shaking out on noise.
executed.outcome_notes: USO drifted steadily higher into the scheduled exit, consistent with a market that continued to price geopolitical risk premium without a resolution catalyst. Price action was constructive — no sharp retracements that would have tested the wider stop — suggesting the momentum signal rather than any single headline drove the gain. Exit was time-based, not triggered by thesis invalidation.
executed.risks_observed: A single-name crude proxy concentrates headline risk: any unexpected de-escalation (ceasefire signal, diplomatic statement) could have reversed the premium sharply intraday, and a scheduled exit offers no protection against that gap. With no correlated hedges in the basket, a broad risk-off commodity sell-off would have hit the position without an offset. Hindsight flag: RSI at 62 on entry left limited buffer before overbought territory, compressing the asymmetry of the trade.

executed.thesis: Oil supply shock confirmed by IEA (commercial inventories depleting rapidly with weeks left) and corroborated by price action well above SMA20 ($138.57) and SMA50 ($128.01) with RSI 61.6. Iran deal risk is real but incomplete — US proposal is a temporary OFAC waiver, Iran demands full sanctions removal — leaving supply-tightness thesis intact for today's session.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly from entry to exit without meaningful retracement, consistent with sustained supply-tightness rather than a spike-and-fade pattern. The scheduled exit captured a 1.46% move; no adverse intraday reversal forced early closure, suggesting the IEA inventory signal held through the session. Exit was time-driven rather than thesis-invalidating, so the underlying catalyst remained live at close.
executed.risks_observed: Iran deal tail risk was acknowledged at entry but not hedged — a surprise diplomatic breakthrough intraday could have reversed the move sharply, and the scheduled exit provided no downside stop if that had occurred. Single-name commodity ETF concentration with no correlated short (e.g., refiner or demand-side offset) left the position fully exposed to any macro risk-off rotation that tends to hit energy alongside equities. RSI near 62 at entry left room for momentum exhaustion; a stronger reading would have flagged more crowding risk in the name.

active.description:
Deterministic baseline. Buys top-N highest previous-day % gainers from the
configured universe, equal weight, no stops, no take-profits. No LLM
involvement. Region-agnostic — runs against S&P 500 in the US pipeline and
against UK + EU blue chips in the UK/EU pipeline. The yardstick every
other strategy must beat in each region.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+735.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was flat on the day with no follow-through on the prior-session surge, and the position ran to scheduled close without hitting any target. The thesis failed: a +735% close-to-open move at this price level ($0.17 sub-penny range) generated zero continuation, suggesting the prior move was exhausted or illiquidity-driven with no real buyers present.
executed.risks_observed: Sub-penny micro-cap with extreme prior-day volatility is a red flag for pump-and-dump dynamics where the move is already over by open. The loss here is purely friction (spread/commission/FX), but the same structure at larger size would have compounded that friction with no upside offset. No liquidity filter meant entry into a market with no meaningful bid.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+400.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Reported entry and exit both at $0.00 with a £-584 loss — the price data is almost certainly truncated at two decimal places and the real prices are fractional cents, but the loss magnitude suggests either a wide spread on exit or a meaningful intraday decline within the sub-cent range. No price continuation occurred and the position was closed on schedule.
executed.risks_observed: A £-584 loss on a stock showing $0.00 entry is a data integrity failure that makes post-trade review nearly impossible; the strategy needs minimum price and minimum tick-size filters to avoid securities where displayed prices carry no information. At this price level, the entire loss is likely spread absorption on entry and/or exit, not directional movement — that's a structural drain with no path to recovery.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+400.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Identical profile to JEWL: $0.00 displayed prices, £-584 loss, scheduled exit with zero price follow-through. TBLT had a prior-day +400% move and gave back nothing and gained nothing visible at this resolution — momentum did not carry.
executed.risks_observed: Running two positions with near-identical structure (same displayed price, same P&L, same lot size, same exit reason) on the same day doubles the concentration in the same failure mode. If these stocks share a sector catalyst or promoter, they are likely correlated and a filter excluding securities below a minimum price (e.g. $0.01) would have screened both. The basket-level loss from just these two names alone is outsized relative to any realistic upside at sub-cent prices.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+163.16% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price held flat at $0.02 intraday with no directional move after a +163% prior-day gain; the position expired at the scheduled close. Friction (spread, FX) accounts for the entire loss, and the thesis found no expression in price action on the day.
executed.risks_observed: At $0.02 the spread as a percentage of price is enormous and any round-trip will be negative in expectation without a meaningful directional move. A +163% prior-day move at this price level is likely a single large trade or thin-market artifact rather than genuine demand, which the flat follow-through confirms.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+138.10% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Closed near flat at +0.00%. Drifted sideways through the session — no follow-through but no meaningful reversal either.
executed.risks_observed: The rule-based control can't distinguish 'rallying on solid fundamentals' from 'rallying on a squeeze about to unwind.' This loss validates the case for news-aware and mean-reverter strategies that would have filtered it.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+200.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was completely flat from entry to scheduled exit; the +200% prior-session spike produced zero follow-through on day 2. The thesis that prior-day strength predicts continuation failed immediately — the move was already exhausted at open.
executed.risks_observed: At $0.15 with no liquidity filter, the entire loss is attributable to spread and transaction costs rather than adverse price movement. Sub-penny-adjacent stocks have proportionally enormous spreads that make any round-trip structurally negative without a significant directional move.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+199.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: No price movement at $0.03 through the scheduled exit; a +199% prior-day spike generated no day-2 momentum. At this price tier a single tick is a 33% move, so 'flat' here means the stock was effectively untradeable as a momentum vehicle.
executed.risks_observed: FAASF carries an F-suffix indicating OTC/foreign-registered stock, adding settlement and liquidity risk on top of the near-zero price problem. This was the second-largest absolute loss despite nominally flat prices, reflecting the structural cost drag at sub-$0.05 levels.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+160.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Entry and exit are both recorded as $0.00, yet the position generated £-115.87 in losses — the largest in the session. A $0.00 fill is not a valid market price; this trade either executed at a sub-penny fraction that rounded to zero or reflects a data pipeline error upstream.
executed.risks_observed: The $0.00 entry price exposes a critical missing safeguard: the strategy has no minimum-price gate that would reject fills at economically nonsensical levels. Sizing in notional currency terms against a $0.00 price creates unbounded share-count exposure and makes the actual risk taken on this leg essentially unquantifiable.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+147.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Flat from entry to scheduled close with no price action in either direction; the +147% prior-session move found no day-2 buyers. The rule had no way to distinguish a stock resting before continuation from one that had fully reverted.
executed.risks_observed: All four basket names today were sub-$1 micro-caps that had already made their entire move the prior session — the basket was structurally concentrated in 'post-spike penny stock' as a single risk factor. Any real adverse move on any one name would have been catastrophic; the flat outcome masked that the selection process is systematically buying into spent momentum with no diversification across regime type.

active.description:
Deterministic baseline. Buys top-N highest previous-day % gainers from the
configured universe, equal weight, no stops, no take-profits. No LLM
involvement. Region-agnostic — runs against S&P 500 in the US pipeline and
against UK + EU blue chips in the UK/EU pipeline. The yardstick every
other strategy must beat in each region.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+45.83% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was flat from entry to scheduled exit — the prior-day +45.83% gap found no continuation intraday, and the entire P&L is transaction cost. The thesis (momentum continuation) was simply absent; the move was fully priced at open.
executed.risks_observed: A 45% prior-day gapper in a low-liquidity UK small-cap carries extreme spread risk at the open; entering at market likely widened the effective cost significantly. No stop or mean-reversion guard meant the position sat through the full session with no exit optionality.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+28.65% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Flat exit at a £0.06 penny stock — at this price level the bid-ask spread alone can represent 5–10% of entry, so the reported 0.00% move likely masks an adverse fill. No continuation of the prior +28.65% gap.
executed.risks_observed: Sub-penny stocks are structurally dangerous for this strategy: minimum tick size is a large percentage of price, liquidity is thin, and the recorded entry/exit price may not reflect actual execution quality. The £-10 flat loss here understates real slippage risk.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+21.43% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: ALTAI.PA exited flat on schedule with no intraday continuation. The slightly higher absolute loss (£-12.10 vs £-10) relative to the other positions is consistent with EUR/GBP FX conversion friction on a Paris-listed name.
executed.risks_observed: Cross-currency exposure adds a hidden cost layer that the per-trade sizing doesn't account for. On a day where all five positions in the basket were flat, the FX drag is proportionally the largest differentiator — a structural inefficiency for small GBP-denominated positions in EUR markets.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+21.21% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Entry and exit both recorded at $0.00, which strongly suggests this position was never actually filled — either the order was rejected, the stock was suspended, or there is a data pipeline recording failure. The £-10 loss is then purely a commission or attempt cost.
executed.risks_observed: A $0.00 fill price is a data integrity red flag that should trigger an alert, not a silent scheduled exit. Without a fill-validation check, the strategy can book losses on phantom positions and misrepresent its actual market exposure.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+20.59% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Same $0.00 entry/exit pattern as EXR.L — position almost certainly was not executed. The prior-day +20.59% gain on NFX.L may have left it halted or illiquid at the open, preventing a real fill.
executed.risks_observed: Two positions in the same basket recording $0.00 prices on the same day points to a systemic gap: the strategy has no pre-entry liquidity or halt check, and no post-fill confirmation before treating a trade as open. At the basket level, this day's exposure was effectively concentrated in only three of five intended positions.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+100.00% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price reversed sharply on the day following a +100% gap, giving back the bulk of the prior move with no intraday recovery. executed.risks_observed: No stop or profit target means the strategy absorbs intraday drawdowns silently — the flat close could mask a significant intraday excursion that recovered by the scheduled exit time. At the basket level, holding three European names simultaneously (TEP.PA, WKL.AS, CAP.PA) creates latent correlation risk if a macro catalyst hits mid-session.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+3.87% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Entry and scheduled exit both at the same price; the gap stalled immediately with no follow-through. Wolters Kluwer's gap was the smallest of the European names in the basket, and the lack of any movement suggests the prior-session move was already fully absorbed at the open.
executed.risks_observed: WKL.AS correlates closely with CAP.PA and other European data/software names also in this basket, meaning the three Paris/Amsterdam positions are not independent bets — a sector-level sell-off would hit all three simultaneously with no diversification benefit.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+3.82% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Price pinned at the round €100.00 level from entry to scheduled exit with no intraday resolution. The round number likely attracted both buyers and sellers in equal measure, suppressing movement and making this day's data point uninformative for evaluating the momentum rule.
executed.risks_observed: Round-number anchoring at €100 can mask intraday volatility that nets to zero by close; the scheduled exit with no intraday monitoring means the strategy would have sat through any dip and recovery without acting. Capgemini's size means it is index-weight sensitive — any passive rebalancing flow on this date could have driven the temporary stability.

executed.thesis: Top previous-day gainer (+3.06% close-to-open). Rule-based control: buying the prior session's strongest movers with no further filter.
executed.outcome_notes: Flat close at the sub-£1 entry price; the gap failed to extend but also held, giving no directional edge. At this price level, a 0.00% nominal outcome may actually represent a small net loss once spread is accounted for.
executed.risks_observed: Sub-penny spread as a fraction of notional is materially higher for JD.L at £0.72 than for the European names in this basket, making transaction costs a disproportionate headwind that the flat P&L figure obscures. The UK-listed name also introduces GBP/EUR cross-rate noise when evaluating basket-level performance against the two Paris and one Amsterdam positions.

active.description:
LLM-driven. Reads the weekly macro view first; only buys stocks in sectors
the macro agent is bullish on; avoids bearish sectors. Regime-aware top-down
strategy. Region-agnostic — the macro view is global, just the candidate
universe differs per region.

executed.thesis: XLK is the undisputed macro leader and PLTR has a specific, fresh catalyst today — an on-premises AI OS deal with Dell announced this morning — hitting a technically clean setup with RSI 67.7 and MACD histogram just crossing positive after a period in negative territory. The combination of dated catalyst, reasonable RSI (not extended), and elevated volume (2.04x) makes this the clearest risk/reward in today's candidate set.
executed.outcome_notes: The Dell AI OS partnership drove immediate and sustained price action; the midday take-profit triggered cleanly, capturing the initial repricing leg without overstaying. The 2.04x volume confirmed institutional participation on the news rather than retail noise, validating that the catalyst had enough weight to move the stock on the day.
executed.risks_observed: At RSI 67.7 on entry, the position had limited technical cushion — any macro rotation or profit-taking wave in XLK could have reversed the move before take-profit triggered. The catalyst was also narrow (a single Dell deal rather than a broad contract win or earnings beat), so a competing headline or negative read-through from the AI infrastructure space would have undercut it quickly.

executed.thesis: NVIDIA's Computex keynote today names Oracle as a major adopter of the new AI-focused processor, directly reinforcing ORCL's cloud AI infrastructure positioning at above-average volume (1.93x); RSI 74.6 is elevated but both SMAs remain well below current price, and the NVIDIA catalyst justifies a 1-day event-driven hold at a tight take-profit.
executed.outcome_notes: The NVIDIA Computex naming of Oracle triggered a sharp, sustained gap that hit the take-profit target well before midday — the cleanest catalyst-to-exit execution in the basket. Above-average volume confirmed the market immediately repriced Oracle's AI cloud positioning rather than treating the Computex mention as noise.
executed.risks_observed: Entry at RSI 74.6 left almost no technical buffer for a 'buy-the-rumour, sell-the-news' reversal, which was a live risk given how extended the stock already was before the keynote. At 8.5% gain, ORCL was the dominant P&L driver for the session, meaning the basket's daily result was heavily concentrated in a single event-driven name — had the Computex read-through disappointed or been overshadowed by a competitor announcement, the whole day's book would have looked very different.

executed.thesis: Rocket Lab has the cleanest technical setup of any unextended candidate at RSI 67.5 with both SMAs well below price and a confirmed +73.89% 20d uptrend; NASA and UFO space ETF inflows driven by SpaceX IPO anticipation provide a durable sector bid that should sustain momentum over 2 sessions, with the wider stop/TP reflecting RKLB's higher per-share volatility.

XLK macro-bullish backdrop aligns directly with IREN's AI infrastructure role; the $3.6B NVIDIA chip financing by Microsoft partner IREN is a genuine step-change catalyst (not priced in at RSI 61 with volume 0.82x), and Cantor's PT raise to $99 anchors 55% fundamental upside from the $64 base.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower from entry and never recovered, exiting at the scheduled close with no upside realised from the financing catalyst or analyst PT raise. The NVIDIA chip deal and Cantor upgrade were both pre-session events, and the 0.82x volume suggested the market had already absorbed them — there was no fresh buying pressure to anchor the thesis intraday.
executed.risks_observed: A scheduled exit with no stop meant the position held through a losing session with no dynamic protection; the loss was small only because the drift was contained. IREN shared AI-infrastructure correlation with PLTR and ORCL in the same basket, so a sector reversal would have compounded losses across all three simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Technology sector leads the week (+5.48%) and ARM sits at the architecture layer of the AI compute stack that Dell's blowout earnings confirm is accelerating; street-high PT raised to $360 provides fresh institutional sponsorship for a gap-continuation move at RSI 75.4.
executed.outcome_notes: Price reversed immediately after entry and trended down to the stop, suggesting the Dell-earnings momentum had already been priced in by the time the position was opened. An RSI of 75.4 at entry meant there was no technical cushion when institutional sellers used the gap-up open as an exit.
executed.risks_observed: Entering a high-RSI momentum name the day after a catalyst is a known fade setup — the street-high PT raise likely marked peak near-term sponsorship rather than the start of a new leg. ARM and SMCI both stopped out on the same thesis (AI infrastructure read-through), creating a correlated double-loss that concentrated drawdown in one narrative.

executed.thesis: Dell's AI server beat is the clearest read-through for SMCI's rack-scale AI infrastructure business; yesterday's Taiwan compliance alliance removes the last key supply-chain overhang while volume 1.72x confirms the 10% surge had real institutional participation.
executed.outcome_notes: The Dell read-through did not translate into sustained buying; price faded through the stop, indicating either the move had already discounted the catalyst or sector rotation out of small-cap AI hardware outweighed the fundamental case. The prior-day 10% volume surge appears to have been distribution rather than accumulation.
executed.risks_observed: SMCI carries persistent governance overhang (accounting restatements, auditor history) that makes it structurally prone to sharp reversals on risk-off days regardless of the fundamental narrative. Running SMCI and ARM simultaneously as AI-infrastructure plays doubled correlated exposure — when the theme didn't follow through, both legs hit stops on the same session.

executed.thesis: Amphenol's MACD histogram just turned from negative to positive at RSI 63 — a cleaner technical entry than extended peers — and as the dominant AI data centre connector supplier, the Dell infrastructure surge translates directly into accelerated order flow; XLK macro-bullish regime provides the tailwind.
executed.outcome_notes: Price edged higher and closed modestly in profit at the scheduled exit, consistent with a beta ride on the XLK tailwind rather than any APH-specific catalyst firing. The MACD flip held but generated no acceleration — the gain tracks the broad sector move rather than anything connective-component-specific.
executed.risks_observed: With no discrete near-term catalyst, APH was the most purely macro-dependent name in the basket, making it the first to give back gains if XLK weakened intraday. Supplier-concentration risk also applies: the Dell infrastructure linkage is real but indirect, and single-session price action provides no signal on order-book dynamics that actually drive APH's earnings revisions.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK Mildly Bullish macro confirmed at +6.46% 5d) with the strongest idiosyncratic catalyst in the pool: record Q1 revenue of $2.42B, strong Q2 guidance, and 2.1x institutional volume confirm this is a genuine earnings re-rating rather than macro momentum; three independent analyst PT raises today ($240–$275) provide layered upside confirmation. AI custom silicon and networking sits outside the bearish memory/storage bucket flagged in today's news brief.
executed.outcome_notes: Earnings re-rating played out as modelled — the combination of beat-and-raise and same-day analyst target lifts provided layered buying pressure that sustained momentum through to the take-profit. Price action was orderly rather than gappy, implying the move was distribution into strength rather than a one-day event.
executed.risks_observed: Post-earnings momentum in semis can reverse sharply within 48–72 hours if the broader sector rotates or a competitor prints a weak number; holding past the initial session concentrates timing risk. MRVL and IREN in the same basket create implicit AI-silicon sector concentration — a single negative data point (export controls, hyperscaler capex cut) would have correlated both positions against us simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Healthcare (XLV Mildly Bullish) is the macro view's highest-conviction sector, and today's CVS announcement expanding Zepbound coverage is a fresh commercial catalyst for LLY's leading GLP-1 franchise; defensively positioned quality with pricing power means it attracts flows on rate-hike-threat days rather than selling off with high-beta tech.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly to the take-profit level without significant drawdown, confirming the CVS coverage announcement triggered sustained buying rather than a fade. The defensive-quality bid held on a day where rate-sensitive names were under pressure, validating the sector rotation logic.
executed.risks_observed: Single-name concentration in a $1000+ stock amplifies gap risk if any GLP-1 safety headline emerges intraday; the position benefited from a sector tailwind that could reverse sharply on FDA news or competitor data readouts with no warning. Healthcare was the only winner in this basket, which masked overall strategy underperformance on the day.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK Mildly Bullish) with 1.63x volume confirming institutional buying and Needham reiterating Buy at $700 (~23% upside); ad-tech sits outside the mildly-bearish enterprise SaaS category and benefits from the oil-decline consumer spending tailwind, while the positive MACD histogram and RSI 69.3 (room to extend) distinguish it from the overbought semi names.
executed.outcome_notes: Stop triggered, with price failing to hold at entry and declining roughly 5% without a recovery attempt — the 1.63x volume at entry looks more consistent with distribution than accumulation in hindsight. The Needham reiteration provided no near-term price support, suggesting the catalyst lacked the freshness needed to drive immediate re-rating.
executed.risks_observed: RSI 69.3 at entry was close enough to overbought that the 'room to extend' framing was optimistic; a name already elevated on prior momentum has a narrower margin before sellers dominate. The ad-tech insulation argument from enterprise SaaS weakness was thesis-level rather than price-level — when broader XLK sentiment softened, the correlation held regardless of sub-sector narrative. No tiered entry or scaled position sizing meant the full stop loss was realised on a single print.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK, Mildly Bullish macro confirmed at +6.18% 5d) with the freshest material catalyst today: $1.6B Dell Blackwell hardware agreement expanding annualized AI cloud revenue from $3.7B to $4.4B. RSI 59.5 is the healthiest among top performers — room to run before overbought; Paul Tudor Jones adding 57% provides institutional validation. Two-day hold allows full price discovery on this fundamental re-rating.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly to the take-profit level, with the Dell Blackwell contract providing a discrete, dateable catalyst that the market continued to price in over the hold period. The two-day window gave enough time for secondary coverage and institutional flow to compound the initial gap, suggesting the re-rating was genuine rather than a knee-jerk spike.
executed.risks_observed: AI infrastructure names are highly correlated in a risk-off move — any macro shock during the hold would have overwhelmed the idiosyncratic catalyst. PTJ's disclosed position was already public at entry, meaning the institutional validation signal was retrospective rather than predictive; a crowded unwind could accelerate a reversal faster than a standard stop would catch.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK, Mildly Bullish macro) AI datacom connectivity play; above-average volume (1.51x) and RSI 65.6 — the healthiest technical profile among high-momentum semiconductors. BofA's explicit non-bubble thesis for AI semis directly removes the key bear argument and supports the fundamental backdrop.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly to take-profit without meaningful retracement, confirming the elevated volume and RSI were genuine accumulation rather than exhaustion. The AI datacom connectivity narrative held — no adverse news broke the momentum. Textbook thesis execution.
executed.risks_observed: CRDO is thinly traded relative to index names; the 1.51x volume figure that looked constructive at entry can reverse sharply on any sector rotation. Running this alongside MU and LRCX created concentrated semi exposure — a single negative data point (export controls, earnings miss elsewhere in the chain) could have hit all three simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK, Mildly Bullish macro); Goldman raises S&P 500 target to 8,000 citing Micron specifically, $1T milestone attracts institutional FOMO flows, and AI server memory prices up 90% confirm the earnings upgrade cycle is real. Volume 1.23x above average is the strongest participation signal in the group.
executed.outcome_notes: The stop triggered on a ~6% drawdown, meaning price reversed hard against the entry despite the Goldman target raise and memory pricing tailwinds. Analyst upgrades and macro catalysts had likely already been priced in at the $912 entry level, so the trade was buying the announcement rather than the underlying trend.
executed.risks_observed: MU at elevated absolute price levels is extremely sensitive to any guidance ambiguity or broader risk-off moves — institutional FOMO flows can unwind faster than they accumulate. The thesis leaned on multiple external catalysts (analyst note, $1T milestone, server pricing) stacking simultaneously, which is a crowded-trade signal in hindsight; when consensus is this loud, the stop needs to be tighter or the position sized down.

executed.thesis: Technology sector (XLK, Mildly Bullish macro); semiconductor equipment structurally benefits from the AI capex build-out as TSMC, Samsung, and Micron expand capacity. RSI 68.8 and a rising MACD histogram provide the cleanest continuation setup in the group — less overextension than memory names with the same macro tailwind.
executed.outcome_notes: Flat exit on a scheduled close — price went nowhere over the holding period, making this a dead-weight position. The RSI and MACD setup did not translate into any directional follow-through, suggesting the equipment layer lagged while memory names moved first.
executed.risks_observed: LRCX's underperformance relative to the memory names it was supposed to share a tailwind with is a correlation-break worth noting — equipment stocks can decouple from end-demand semis when the market is rotating within the sector rather than buying it wholesale. Holding three XLK names simultaneously amplified sector concentration without adding diversification benefit, and the scheduled exit rather than a trailing stop meant the position had no mechanism to capture upside if the move came late.

executed.thesis: Health Care is the macro view's clearest bullish sector (XLV +3.96% 20d, defensive rotation confirmed on yield relief), and CODX delivers a same-day stock-level catalyst — PCR assay advancement for Bundibugyo virus — on top of that sector tailwind, with pre-market +22.7% confirming the market is pricing the news today. Stop set at roughly 1.5× ATR from expected open to survive intraday noise without full exposure to a gap-fill reversal.
executed.outcome_notes: The pre-market gap filled entirely by the scheduled exit, leaving the trade flat at the entry price. The Bundibugyo PCR catalyst drove a sharp open but attracted no sustained buyers through the session, which is typical for small-cap biotech single-day catalysts where the news is narrow and the float is thin.
executed.risks_observed: The ATR-based stop was explicitly sized to survive intraday noise rather than protect against a full gap-fill, so the risk management design accepted the outcome that occurred — but that means the stop provided no real protection on the primary risk the thesis identified. A catalyst-fade trade in a sub-$10 biotech with no durable sector or index bid is essentially a lottery ticket; the flat exit masked a scenario where the gap-fill could have continued well below entry.

executed.thesis: Energy sector is the macro regime's strongest confirmed bid — XLE +5.77% 20d and supply-shock thesis intact. MPC is the highest-quality expression: Goldman raises PT, record US refined product exports at 7.92m b/d, high refinery utilisation, and RSI 61.9 (not overbought) with clean technical structure above both SMAs.
executed.outcome_notes: MPC declined steadily through the holding period and was exited at the scheduled close with no intraday catalyst to reverse it. The Goldman PT raise and export-volume data were already priced in or insufficient to drive near-term momentum; sector-level XLE strength did not translate to single-stock price appreciation over this window.
executed.risks_observed: No stop on a directional large-cap energy name meant the full drawdown was realized without truncation — the scheduled exit structure provided no downside protection. Combined with WMB, the basket carried two energy or energy-adjacent names that both lost on the same day, revealing meaningful sector concentration even though MPC and WMB were positioned as distinct expressions.

executed.thesis: Consumer Staples is the macro view's second pillar — defensive rotation confirmed with XLP +4.15% 20d. COST is the cleanest expression: new all-time high, UBS raises to $1275, and the direct mechanism (higher gas prices driving traffic to fuel-station anchored warehouses) means the stagflationary macro is a structural tailwind, not just sentiment.
executed.outcome_notes: The stop was triggered, confirming a sharp enough reversal from entry to breach the downside level. Buying into a fresh all-time high on an analyst upgrade is an extended entry; when the broader tape offered no follow-through, mean-reversion from that level moved quickly enough to take out the stop before any recovery.
executed.risks_observed: Entering at an all-time high compresses the distance to any rational stop, making the trade mechanically fragile to even modest reversals — the stop did its job but the setup accepted that risk structurally. The fuel-station traffic mechanism is a multi-month thesis layered onto a stock already pricing in significant optimism, which creates a mismatch between catalyst time horizon and the single-day holding window.

executed.thesis: Midstream natural gas infrastructure diversifies energy exposure away from crude-price Iran headline risk while staying in the bullish energy sector. Morgan Stanley raises PT to $98 (+26% upside) on Overweight — a fresh and specific catalyst on a fee-based business model that insulates from spot oil swings.
executed.outcome_notes: WMB drifted lower and exited at the scheduled close; the Morgan Stanley upgrade and fee-based insulation narrative generated no near-term buying interest sufficient to hold the entry price. The diversification rationale versus crude-price risk did not prevent the name from moving in the same direction as the rest of the energy basket.
executed.risks_observed: The supposed decorrelation from spot oil via fee-based revenues didn't manifest on the day — WMB and MPC both declined, suggesting that on short horizons midstream names still carry substantial correlated energy-sector beta. Two scheduled exits in the same session with no stops on either energy name amplified the realized loss versus what a trailing stop or tighter exit structure would have allowed.

executed.thesis: Upstream E&P exposure completes the energy stack (refiner + midstream + E&P). Citigroup raises PT to $147 with EOG above both SMAs and a healthy RSI 58.7; 2-day hold keeps the horizon short enough to exit before any Iran resolution fully re-prices crude.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the hold and never reclaimed entry, suggesting the Citi upgrade was already priced in or failed to attract incremental buyers within the 2-day window. The scheduled exit captured the loss cleanly with no adverse gap, but the analyst catalyst produced no measurable lift — crude price action was the dominant governor, not the PT revision.
executed.risks_observed: Running refiner, midstream, and E&P simultaneously concentrates the book in a single commodity driver; a crude leg-down hits all three in the same direction with no natural offset. The Iran-resolution tail risk flagged at entry — the very reason for the short horizon — may have weighed on E&P sentiment even without a formal announcement, and there was no stop in place to limit downside if the diplomatic newsflow accelerated mid-hold.

executed.thesis: Agilysys delivered a Q4 double-beat with above-consensus FY27 revenue guidance, driving above-average volume (1.29×) and confirming genuine institutional demand rather than thin-tape drift; Needham reiterates Buy at $120 (34% above close) providing a credible upside anchor. Hospitality software is insulated from the AI-capex-durability concerns dragging semiconductor names, and the earnings catalyst in a risk-off tape marks it as a relative-strength outlier.
executed.outcome_notes: Post-earnings momentum failed to hold beyond the entry session; the broader risk-off tape overwhelmed the single-stock catalyst and price sold through the stop without any intervening recovery. Volume confirmation at entry did not translate into sustained institutional support — the signal described conditions at the open, not over the hold period.
executed.risks_observed: Entering a small/mid-cap software name immediately after an earnings gap concentrates risk at the worst liquidity point: stops on thin-float names in a down tape can gap rather than fill cleanly. The 'insulated from AI-capex concerns' framing was a relative argument that assumed broad sector rotation into quality software, which did not materialise on the day.

executed.thesis: ServiceNow's enterprise workflow automation demand is driven by AI-driven efficiency spend — a more durable capex line than infrastructure buildout — separating it from the AMAT/MU/ORCL capex-durability selloff; the stock is above both SMAs with a strong MACD positive crossover after a +22.67% 5-day run. The 65% cash allocation held back reflects the absence of any Energy, Staples, or Healthcare setup that meets both the macro alignment and technical quality bar simultaneously.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the scheduled hold period with no fresh catalyst to extend the prior 5-day run; the scheduled exit captured the loss rather than a stop cutting it earlier. The AI-efficiency-spend differentiation thesis was directionally reasonable but the entry followed exhausted momentum, and no incremental news arrived to re-engage buyers.
executed.risks_observed: A scheduled exit with no stop meant full downside exposure to drift for the entire hold — asymmetric on the loss side relative to the upside available after a +22% move. Sector-level multiple compression in enterprise software during a risk-off tape pulled the name lower regardless of fundamental differentiation, exposing a correlation assumption that was not stress-tested in the position sizing.

executed.thesis: Energy is the top macro call for W21 — oil +27.7% (20d) in a stagflationary regime directly inflates offshore drilling day rates, and VAL as a pure-play deepwater/harsh-environment operator is the cleanest expression of sustained high oil prices. RSI 70.3 above both SMAs with positive MACD and +25.79% 20d momentum confirm the sector call is being priced in at the stock level.
executed.outcome_notes: VAL held its upward trajectory through the scheduled exit, with the oil macro tailwind continuing to support offshore drillers without meaningful reversal. The scheduled exit captured the move cleanly — no stop pressure, no thesis deterioration, just trend continuation.
executed.risks_observed: At RSI 70+ on entry, any oil sentiment reversal or inventory surprise could have triggered a sharp mean-reversion in an already extended name. Single-commodity dependency means VAL has near-zero diversification value within an energy-heavy basket.

executed.thesis: Healthcare is rated mildly bullish as defensive rotation re-asserts with quality premium attractive in an uncertain stagflationary regime; BIO has the added stock-level catalyst of Elliott Management building a large activist stake announced today, providing institutional support and a catalyst for operational improvements from a mid-50s RSI that is not yet overbought.
executed.outcome_notes: BIO was the strongest performer in the basket, with the Elliott activist catalyst providing a durable bid that carried through the holding period. Price action confirmed institutional accumulation rather than a fade, validating the event-driven overlay on top of the sector rotation call.
executed.risks_observed: Activist-driven moves can unwind abruptly if the stake is leaked to be smaller than reported, hedged, or if Elliott signals disengagement — the catalyst is binary and not sector-correlated, making it harder to hedge. Sizing this alongside macro defensives creates a mixed-signal position that behaves differently from the rest of the healthcare allocation under stress.

executed.thesis: Technology sector is mildly bullish and oil-price surge creates a secondary narrative tailwind for distributed solar as an alternative-energy beneficiary; ENPH shows the strongest technical confirmation of any Tech candidate with RSI 71.5, +32.72% 5d and +47.49% 20d above both SMAs, with no company-specific negative news to fade the move.
executed.outcome_notes: ENPH effectively went nowhere, with the exit nearly flat despite the strong technical setup on entry — the oil-as-solar-tailwind narrative did not translate into incremental buying during the holding period. The position was dead weight: extended technicals stalled rather than resolved higher.
executed.risks_observed: Entering a name at RSI 71.5 and +47% 20d momentum with a narrative-driven rather than fundamental thesis is a timing risk — momentum exhaustion is the base case, not the edge case. The indirect relationship between oil prices and ENPH demand is too weak a catalyst to sustain a breakout from an already overbought level, and this trade flagged that risk clearly in hindsight.

executed.thesis: Technology is macro-rated bullish on the AI capex supercycle; NVIDIA's fresh 7.8M-share stake in Coherent is a direct, high-conviction catalyst confirming the photonics/optical-interconnect bottleneck narrative. RSI 63.3 and an expanding MACD histogram (+4.68) leave room to run without being overbought, and price is well clear of both SMAs.
executed.outcome_notes: The position was closed at the scheduled time with no price movement captured. The NVIDIA stake catalyst did not generate intraday follow-through during the holding window, suggesting the announcement was already absorbed into price at entry — the signal was real but the timing was late relative to when the market priced it.
executed.risks_observed: Single-catalyst dependence on a disclosed institutional stake creates event-risk concentration: once the filing is public, the edge is thin and the window short. Both COHR and VRT in the same basket share AI-capex exposure, so any macro or sentiment reversal in that theme would have hit both legs simultaneously with no natural hedge.

executed.thesis: Industrials are mildly bullish via reshoring/infrastructure spend, and Vertiv's AI data-centre power and cooling infrastructure gives it a direct co-exposure to the same capex cycle as tech; three analyst upgrades this week (BofA $440, RBC $435, Barclays $412 vs $371 close) confirm the fundamental re-rating. RSI 69.3 and positive MACD support continued momentum with the $440 BofA target as the natural profit objective.
executed.outcome_notes: Closed flat at the scheduled exit, capturing none of the analyst-upgrade re-rating. Three upgrades in a single week often signals a coordinated view that is already partially priced by the time retail and systematic flows arrive; the $440 BofA target remained a valid destination but required a time horizon the scheduled exit could not accommodate.
executed.risks_observed: RSI at 69.3 on entry left almost no buffer before overbought territory — any intraday rotation out of industrials would have pushed the position into the red before the scheduled close, with no stop in place to limit it. Correlation with COHR in the same session means the basket had two correlated AI-infrastructure longs with a combined unhedged sector bet.

executed.thesis: Energy is the strongest sector this week (+6.71% 5d) and the commodity supercycle narrative is gaining traction in news flow; TRGP's midstream infrastructure model delivers energy exposure with stable, fee-based cash flows that are less sensitive to oil price volatility, backed by RSI 69.6, expanding MACD, and the highest volume ratio (1.49x) among energy candidates.
executed.outcome_notes: Exited at the scheduled time with no gain despite entering the week's top-performing sector. A +6.71% five-day sector move often precedes a consolidation day rather than extension; the scheduled exit removed any ability to distinguish between a pause and a reversal, locking in neither profit nor a defensive cut.
executed.risks_observed: Entering a momentum name after a multi-day run means price can sit flat or retrace even when the underlying thesis is intact — the fee-based model reduces oil-price sensitivity but not entry-timing risk. The highest volume ratio in the energy screen (1.49x) could equally indicate distribution rather than accumulation; without a volume-direction check, it was an ambiguous signal.

active.description:
LLM-driven. Reads the weekly macro view first; only buys stocks in sectors
the macro agent is bullish on; avoids bearish sectors. Regime-aware top-down
strategy. Region-agnostic — the macro view is global, just the candidate
universe differs per region.

executed.thesis: Technology is the top macro sector (Bullish, +19.76% 20d) driven by AI capex revival and falling yields as a DCF tailwind; BESI's semiconductor equipment exposure to AI advanced packaging sits at the centre of this cycle, with RSI 66.5, expanding MACD, and price firmly above both 20/50-day SMAs confirming the uptrend is intact.
executed.outcome_notes: T212 paper portfolio was reset on 2026-06-01 (platform-level reset by user). Position was force-cleared in the ledger because the broker-side state was wiped; no real fill price was captured. Treat P&L as missing for evaluation.
executed.risks_observed: Real fill price not captured because the platform reset preceded the close.

executed.thesis: Materials sector is Mildly Bullish as base metals benefit from dollar weakness (DXY -0.28% this week) and the growth-revival rotation away from defensives; ArcelorMittal's +20.47% 20d momentum with RSI 66.8 and volume 1.70x average confirms institutional re-rating of steel at the low cost of 0.30% round-trip.
