executed.thesis: Consumer Discretionary is Mildly Bullish on the macro view with oil's collapse (USO -12.24% from 20d ago) directly compressing jet fuel costs — IAG is the highest-operating-leverage expression of that tailwind; +10.08% 5d, RSI 64.6, and strong positive relative strength vs ISF (+10.38% 5d) confirm the airline re-rating is actively in progress.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the holding window and the scheduled exit crystallised the loss, with no intraday momentum to extend the preceding 5-day run. Entering after a +10% move with RSI near 65 meant the re-rating was largely priced in at entry; the oil-cost tailwind was a known macro narrative rather than a fresh catalyst capable of driving same-session continuation.
executed.risks_observed: No stop-loss left the only exit trigger as time, so any intraday reversal in airline sentiment ran unhedged for the full window. Holding this alongside a second macro-theme momentum name on the same day concentrated book risk in positions that had already made large prior moves — both prone to mean-reversion if the broader tape softened.

executed.thesis: Materials Mildly Bullish; Anglo American's copper and PGM exposure aligns directly with today's energy-transition metals squeeze narrative (gallium restrictions tightening, copper demand accelerating), and the +5.00% 5d with RSI 61.6 above both SMAs shows the market is already pricing the theme.
executed.outcome_notes: Price slipped modestly from entry to scheduled exit with no meaningful price action to justify the metals-transition narrative on the day. The +5% 5d move and above-SMA positioning at entry suggest the copper/PGM squeeze was already a consensus trade; there were insufficient incremental buyers to extend it further within the holding window.
executed.risks_observed: Like the concurrent IAG position, the only active risk control here was the scheduled exit — no stop beneath the thesis meant the strategy was fully exposed to a metals-sentiment reversal with no circuit-breaker. At the basket level, both trades on the day were momentum entries taken after sizeable prior moves, structurally skewing the book toward continuation risk rather than mean-reversion protection.

executed.thesis: BE Semiconductor is a direct beneficiary of the AI capex cycle in the macro's top-rated bullish sector; above-average volume (1.33x) with MACD expanding and clean break above both SMAs confirms institutional demand. Semiconductor equipment names respond with a lag to AI platform wins, keeping this catalyst fresh.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the holding period and exited scheduled rather than at a target or stop, indicating the momentum signals did not translate into sustained buying. The MACD expansion and SMA break likely reflected a short-lived burst; follow-through was absent, possibly as broader semiconductor equipment names faced profit-taking or macro headwinds overshadowed the AI capex narrative on the day.
executed.risks_observed: High-beta semiconductor equipment names amplify any rotation away from AI-adjacent names, and without an intraday stop the full drawdown was absorbed passively. The volume confirmation at entry was a one-bar signal with no mechanical exit to protect it — a trailing stop or time-stop with a tighter floor would have limited exposure once price reversed below the entry SMA.

executed.thesis: Financials are macro-neutral but ABN AMRO's MACD histogram is expanding (+0.241) with the strongest 20d momentum in the sector (+15.24%), and ECB holding rates preserves NIM. Low round-trip cost (0.30%) and near-normal volume make this the most cost-efficient route to partial diversification outside the tech concentration.
executed.outcome_notes: Price edged modestly higher through the scheduled hold, capturing a small positive drift consistent with the momentum setup but well short of any breakout. The ECB backdrop held, confirming the macro premise, though the gain was incremental rather than driven by any identifiable intraday catalyst.
executed.risks_observed: Both BESI and ABN are AEX-listed, so an Amsterdam-or-EU-wide sell-off would hit both legs simultaneously and neutralise the diversification intent — the correlation between Dutch large-caps in a risk-off session is non-trivial. The ABN gain at +0.59% covered only a fraction of the BESI loss, exposing the basket to a net negative even when the 'diversifier' worked as designed.

executed.thesis: Technology is the strongest 5d sector (+6.46%) confirming the bullish macro call, and Infineon specifically benefits from today's GaN/AI power design news (Navitas/PCIM) as a direct European semiconductor play. MACD histogram positive (+0.822) despite extended RSI; reduced allocation versus peers acknowledges the overbought condition and yesterday's ASML mean-reversion lesson.
executed.outcome_notes: Price ground higher through the session and the scheduled exit captured the move cleanly, confirming that the sector bid was genuine and the AI-power catalyst provided at least intraday support. The reduced allocation versus peers was the right call given the elevated RSI — full size would have added risk without proportionally more return given the modest absolute move.
executed.risks_observed: The trade was entirely dependent on a single-session event catalyst; had the Navitas/PCIM news been absorbed by open or reversed on profit-taking, the overbought RSI left little technical buffer. No stop meant full exposure to a sharp intraday reversal, and the scheduled exit rather than a trailing mechanism likely left some of the move uncaptured.

executed.thesis: Financials are mildly bullish in today's news brief with the 97bp NIM spread providing a structural tailwind in the macro view. BBVA is the strongest-setup financials name: highest volume ratio (0.89) confirming participation, MACD histogram positive, RSI 62.6, and the lowest round-trip cost (0.30%) among European bank candidates.
executed.outcome_notes: Price went nowhere — the one-pip adverse close was entirely noise, and the financials macro theme produced no measurable intraday move in BBVA. The structural NIM argument is a multi-week driver, not a same-session catalyst, so the flat outcome reflects a thesis/timeframe mismatch rather than thesis failure.
executed.risks_observed: A 'mildly bullish' sector tag was a thin foundation for a one-day hold; the absence of a same-day catalyst meant the trade was essentially a passive sector bet with round-trip costs eating any drift. Across the basket, all three exits were scheduled, so correlation between flat-to-up names and a genuinely flat name compressed the basket's dispersion — a losing day in macro conditions would have hit all three simultaneously with no offsetting dynamic stop behaviour.

executed.thesis: Consumer discretionary is mildly bullish today on Iran-US peace progress lifting risk appetite to market all-time highs. Adidas shows clean MACD momentum (+1.071 histogram), RSI 67.1 with room to run, and the broader discretionary upgrade narrative (Crocs, Deckers, Wolverine all up same session) confirms the sector bid is real, not idiosyncratic.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly in the intended direction through the session, consistent with the broad discretionary sector lift. The scheduled exit collected the gain without incident, and the multi-name sector confirmation (Crocs, Deckers etc.) meant the move was not idiosyncratic noise.
executed.risks_observed: The Iran-US geopolitical catalyst is fragile and binary — any headline reversal mid-session would have hit a stock already near overbought levels with no stop in place. IFX.DE and ADS.DE are both German-listed risk-on names, so the basket carried implicit DAX concentration: a Germany-specific shock (energy, FX, macro data) would have correlated both positions against the strategy simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Technology sector is macro-aligned Mildly Bullish with AI capex narrative intact and XLK +6.18% 5d confirming the call. ASML leads the European tech universe with strongest 5d relative strength vs EXSA.DE (+8.79%), RSI at a non-extreme 65.2, and MACD histogram firmly positive at +11.85 — the cleanest expression of the semiconductor capex supercycle.
executed.outcome_notes: Price declined ~2.4% from entry to scheduled exit, with no stop triggered — the drawdown was absorbed passively across the hold window. The bull thesis failed to materialise despite the strong 5-day setup, suggesting the entry captured late-stage momentum rather than the start of a fresh leg. Mean reversion after the extended prior run (+8.79% 5d) was the most likely driver.
executed.risks_observed: Entering after a significant 5-day surge elevated mean-reversion risk that was not offset by any trailing stop or time-stop recalibration. Both tech positions (ASML + ADYEN) printed losses on the same session, confirming correlated sector-level headwinds dominated idiosyncratic stock signals; single-sector concentration amplified the damage.

executed.thesis: Technology sector Mildly Bullish; ADYEN's MACD histogram expanded to +4.29 (strongest expansion in the tech sub-group excluding ASML), RSI at a healthy 61.3 leaving room to run, and the yield easing this week is a marginal positive for growth/fintech valuations. Chosen over BESI due to less extended RSI and better MACD dynamics.
executed.outcome_notes: Essentially flat loss with no momentum follow-through from either the MACD expansion signal or the yield-easing tailwind. The scheduled exit removed any opportunity for the thesis to play out over a longer window, and no intraday catalyst bridged the gap.
executed.risks_observed: Both tech positions moved against the basket simultaneously, exposing the high intra-basket correlation; a sector-level event would have hit this name regardless of its superior MACD/RSI profile relative to peers. The yield easing tailwind is a multi-session macro driver that is structurally mismatched to a short holding window, inflating conviction without adding near-term edge.

executed.thesis: Financials sector Neutral with yield-curve NIM tailwind intact (97bp spread) and benign credit; DBK shows the cleanest MACD histogram expansion (+0.219) in the European bank group on a +8.83% 5d run, and the 0.30% round-trip cost means only 0.60% predicted return needed to clear the gate.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was virtually unchanged from entry to scheduled exit despite the strong prior 5-day run and favourable MACD signal, consistent with momentum stalling after the move rather than continuing. The NIM spread and benign credit backdrop remained intact but generated no price action within the hold period.
executed.risks_observed: The strategy's own minimum predicted return threshold (0.60% net of costs) flagged this as a marginal inclusion; the flat outcome confirms the trade was at or below the edge of viability, and round-trip costs eroded even a breakeven result. With such a thin margin of safety, any adverse tick or wider spread at execution would have turned this into a loss — the low-conviction gate should probably be set higher.

executed.thesis: Healthcare is macro-aligned as a defensive play in today's risk-off session (Nvidia miss + hawkish central banks); LLY.DE adds a stock-specific catalyst with Phase 3 retatrutide showing 28.3% weight loss and the Engage Biologics acquisition extending the pipeline, creating a genuine re-rating event on top of the sector defensive bid. Two-day hold allows full price discovery on news published after yesterday's close.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved steadily through the session and held gains into the scheduled close, suggesting the defensive bid was real and the retatrutide news continued to find buyers rather than fading intraday. The scheduled exit captured the move cleanly — no evidence of a stop hunt or mean-reversion that would have argued for an earlier exit.
executed.risks_observed: EUR/GBP translation drag was a latent headwind throughout; a weaker euro on the day would have meaningfully compressed the sterling return. Clinical-stage re-rating events can reverse sharply on analyst downgrades or secondary data reads, and the two-day hold window left no dynamic exit mechanism if sentiment shifted overnight.

executed.thesis: Energy is the strongest macro sector and oil holds above $100 on Hormuz geopolitical premium with Iran talks unresolved; Repsol adds a stock-specific bid via Pikka Alaska Phase 1 production startup, and its FX-only 0.30% round-trip cost structure means the cost gate is cleared at materially lower returns than stamp-duty LSE energy names, improving the risk/reward ratio.
executed.outcome_notes: The oil macro backdrop held but Repsol moved against the trade regardless, implying the stock was responding to something other than spot price — likely European refining margin compression or general Spain/EM equity outflows on the risk-off day. The scheduled exit enforced a full hold through a losing position rather than allowing a cut when the stock diverged from the sector early in the session.
executed.risks_observed: Holding energy equity as an oil proxy in a risk-off session is structurally inconsistent — equities carry balance-sheet and sentiment risk that crude futures don't, and that gap widened here. The Pikka startup catalyst was likely stale at entry (production news already circulating), so the stock-specific kicker that was supposed to offset sector noise wasn't fresh enough to generate incremental buyers.

executed.thesis: Direct crude oil exposure in the highest-conviction macro sector; above-average volume (1.48x) alongside healthy RSI 59.5 and positive MACD histogram confirms institutional rather than retail participation, and oil holding above $100 on Hormuz premium provides a natural intraday support floor. One-day hold keeps the cost gate at +1.00%, which the energy thesis comfortably clears.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted 0.75% lower from entry and was closed at the scheduled end-of-day exit with no intervening stop or target trigger. The volume and momentum signals did not translate into intraday follow-through, suggesting the Hormuz-premium bid had already been absorbed before entry rather than providing a continuing tailwind. Exiting on schedule rather than on price action means the strategy accepted the full drift loss passively.
executed.risks_observed: A time-based exit is a blunt instrument on a momentum entry: once the thesis stopped working intraday there was no mechanism to exit early, so the position simply bled to close. CRUP.L as a single-name crude proxy carries basis risk — stock-specific factors (e.g. fund flows, spread widening) can decouple it from spot oil regardless of the macro backdrop. The +1.00% cost gate cited in the thesis left very little margin for any adverse move before the trade was offside.

executed.thesis: Cleanest expression of the Bullish energy macro call: oil +27.7% (20d), Hormuz crisis reshaping global LNG flows, and TotalEnergies expanding Eastern Mediterranean gas exposure all directly support earnings. RSI 56 leaves room to run, MACD just turning positive, and both SMAs confirm the uptrend without the overbought risk seen in other candidates.
executed.outcome_notes: Position closed flat at schedule with zero price movement captured — the macro tailwinds (oil spike, LNG re-routing) did not translate into intraday TTE.PA price action during the hold window. Scheduled exit fired before the thesis had time to express itself; no directional signal confirmed or invalidated.

Holding a Hormuz-narrative position through a fixed schedule rather than a catalyst-driven exit increases gap risk around news flow.

executed.thesis: Health care is Mildly Bullish as defensive rotation re-asserts in a stagflationary regime where consumers are squeezed and rate-sensitives are under pressure. Merck KGaA offers quality defensive exposure with an accelerating MACD histogram (+0.843), RSI 56 (ample room), and no overbought risk despite the broader market selling off on oil/yield concerns.
executed.outcome_notes: Flat exit at schedule; defensive-rotation thesis produced no measurable price response within the hold window. With entry and exit at identical levels, there is no evidence the stagflationary bid for healthcare quality names was active on this session.
executed.risks_observed: Defensive rotation trades are regime-dependent and slow-moving — a scheduled short-duration exit is structurally mismatched to that thesis, creating a pattern where the position absorbs any intraday noise without capturing the multi-day drift it was sized for. Correlation risk with the rest of the basket is low, but the zero-move outcome suggests broader market conditions were not conducive to any of the four positions.

executed.thesis: Financials are Neutral but ABN AMRO carries a clear stock-specific catalyst: a just-reported analyst forecast beat confirmed by 1.79x above-average volume, which distinguishes it from the sector-level drift. The yield-curve steepening (10Y at 4.595%, actively repricing) provides a medium-term NIM tailwind for a bank that is structurally asset-sensitive.
executed.outcome_notes: Catalyst trade (analyst beat + 1.79x volume confirmation) closed flat at schedule with no follow-through. The volume signal did not sustain into a price move, suggesting either the catalyst was already fully priced at entry or liquidity in ABN.AS absorbed the buying without directional resolution.
executed.risks_observed: Volume-confirmed catalyst trades carry the specific risk that the confirming volume *is* the event — once the burst clears, price stalls or fades. Entering after a high-volume beat rather than ahead of it means the informational edge may already be exhausted. A neutral-sector stock-specific trade also lacks a sector tailwind to carry it if the idiosyncratic catalyst loses momentum.

executed.risks_observed: All four basket positions closed at exactly zero P&L on a scheduled exit, which points to a structural issue: the strategy is generating well-reasoned entries but the exit mechanism (time-based schedule) is not aligned with any of the thesis durations — energy macro, defensive rotation, catalyst follow-through, and momentum continuation all operate on different timescales, none of which are a fixed intraday window. The 41.7% prior run in IFX.DE was flagged at entry as a risk and the flat outcome is consistent with a stock that is extended and digesting gains rather than continuing.

active.tier2_thesis: IC 0.303 / n=299 is the only sleeve above the shadow T2 evidence floor (IC ≥ 0.25, n ≥ 200); promoted into the Alpaca slot freed by momentum-trader@us demote so we can stress-test fee-net P&L against the new 2.0x cost gate.

executed.thesis: Reconciled from Alpaca portfolio (slot 1) — original ledger entry missing (likely an entry-run timeout or smart-merge race). Daily exit will close this normally.
executed.outcome_notes: Position was recovered via reconciliation with no recoverable entry rationale, so it's not possible to assess whether a thesis held — the scheduled exit closed it at a modest gain, suggesting CRM drifted constructively through the session without a sharp directional catalyst in either direction.
executed.risks_observed: The core risk here is the reconciliation gap itself: without a documented thesis or stop level, this slot had no defined invalidation point and was managed purely by the daily exit schedule. If CRM had sold off sharply intraday, there was no strategy-layer stop to act on it — the position would have ridden the loss to the scheduled close.

executed.thesis: Dell Q1 FY2027 earnings blowout (+64% surprise, AI server backlog surging with multi-year customer commitments) driving 37-38% premarket gap; Mizuho raising PT to $435 and wave of analyst upgrades confirms institutional re-pricing is fresh and in progress at today's open.

The scheduled exit rather than a stop or target suggests the position simply sat flat; the small negative P&L is pure cost drag, not adverse price action.
executed.risks_observed: Large premarket earnings gaps are a well-known fade setup: by the time the open arrives, institutional re-pricing is largely done and early holders are distributing into retail buyers. There was no hard stop in place, meaning the position was exposed to a meaningful reversal throughout the session with no asymmetric protection on the downside.

executed.thesis: Post-earnings analyst upgrade wave (Barclays $275, JPM $240, UBS $230, Citi $225 vs. $204.83 close) signals deep institutional conviction in AI custom chip demand outlook; spread between current price and consensus targets suggests intraday repricing has further to run.
executed.outcome_notes: Price sold off steadily from entry and hit the stop, suggesting the open acted as a sell-the-news event — the upgrade wave was already priced in pre-market and the open provided liquidity for holders to exit into. The gap between analyst targets and entry price did not translate to intraday repricing pressure; it had already occurred.
executed.risks_observed: Entering at the first print after a heavily covered analyst upgrade cycle carries acute mean-reversion risk: the crowd buying the news at open is often absorbing distribution from those who positioned on the original earnings move. Same-session stop-outs on both MRVL and KTOS point to basket-level correlation — both were high-beta growth names entered on momentum catalysts on the same day, compounding the session loss.

executed.thesis: Trump administration considering equity stakes in domestic drone makers is a fresh May 29 policy catalyst that drove KTOS up 5.84% after-hours; RSI 58.9 and above-SMA20 positioning leaves technical room to extend, and government-backed sector plays sustain momentum through open.
executed.outcome_notes: The after-hours policy catalyst faded immediately at the open: price declined from entry through the stop without recovering, suggesting the 5.84% AH move had already fully priced the news and the open provided exit liquidity for overnight holders. Policy-driven catalysts from informal reports or 'administration considering' language are particularly prone to this pattern.
executed.risks_observed: Soft policy signals ('considering equity stakes') carry high uncertainty and are easily walked back, making them unreliable anchors for a sustained gap continuation thesis. With MRVL also stopped out the same session, the basket ran two correlated high-momentum longs into an environment where buyers weren't stepping in — a day-of context check (broad tape, sector flow) could have flagged the risk before both positions were opened.

executed.thesis: Dell's AI server blowout directly validates HPE's accelerated compute segment thesis, with HPE explicitly named in today's market focus headlines; HPE earnings in 3 days (June 1) adds a pre-earnings catalyst layer creating a 2-session window for institutional positioning.
executed.outcome_notes: The Dell-to-HPE read-across played out cleanly: HPE moved sharply higher intraday and the midday take-profit trigger fired well before any mean-reversion, capturing the bulk of the momentum leg. Price action was consistent with institutional rotation into the accelerated compute names on the back of sector validation rather than HPE-specific news, which kept the move orderly and allowed a clean exit.
executed.risks_observed: Holding into the close would have introduced earnings-gap risk given HPE's report was imminent; the midday exit sidestepped that but the strategy had no explicit pre-earnings stop defined, so the protection was structural (take-profit level) rather than deliberate. The trade was also effectively a leveraged proxy on Dell's beat — any intraday walk-back of the Dell reaction would have compressed HPE faster than the underlying thesis could reassert.

executed.thesis: Q1 double beat with AWS AI partnership expansion filed yesterday — today is the first full session for institutions to reprice; volume at 2.11× confirms active accumulation and analyst consensus of $270-300 vs $175 close implies a large gap still to close.

Despite elevated volume confirming activity, institutional repricing did not arrive on the expected timeline — the large gap between spot and analyst targets may reflect market skepticism about the pace of monetization rather than simply slow absorption.
executed.risks_observed: A $175-vs-$270+ analyst gap is a structural story, not a one-session catalyst; news-reactive edge is thin when the repricing horizon is quarters rather than days. No stop-loss was active, so the downside was bounded only by the scheduled exit — had SNOW sold off on profit-taking after the prior session's move, the position had no defined floor.

executed.thesis: Record Q1 revenue of $2.42B with strong Q2 guidance filed yesterday is still being absorbed as evidenced by 2.10× volume; multiple analysts upgrade targets to $240-275 vs $198.70 close, and the custom ASIC AI demand narrative is fresh.

The 2.10× volume signal correctly identified active repricing rather than exhausted momentum, and the custom-ASIC narrative gave the move a specific, defensible driver.

AI semiconductor names carry binary macro sensitivity: a single negative data center capex headline can reverse a post-earnings drift before take-profit fires.

executed.thesis: Two catalysts firing simultaneously today: the Trump Accounts app launches with Treasury Secretary endorsement (6M enrolled children = direct retail AUM pipeline) and Robinhood Agentic Trading debuts — RSI 48.7 means the stock has not pre-run the news.

Product launch events in retail fintech appear to be treated as adoption stories priced over weeks, not immediate AUM or revenue events.
executed.risks_observed: Stacking two unproven, execution-dependent catalysts amplifies complexity without adding conviction — if the market views either as regulatory or adoption risk rather than a done deal, the combined signal reads as noise. Both drivers require downstream user behavior to translate into revenue, making them structurally misaligned with the news-reactive same-session window.

executed.thesis: Dual strategic announcements disclosed via fresh 8-K this morning — $10B+ quantum R&D/capex commitment and $5B Project Lightwell (20K engineers on AI/open-source security) — arrive on a stock in a confirmed 15% 5-day uptrend, extending the narrative with new institutional-grade commitments.
executed.outcome_notes: The dual 8-K announcements (quantum capex and Project Lightwell) produced zero net movement despite an entry into a confirmed uptrend; the market apparently absorbed or discounted the disclosures within minutes, not over a full session. Multi-year R&D commitments with headcount pledges are routinely treated as aspirational signaling by large-cap investors rather than near-term earnings catalysts.
executed.risks_observed: IBM announcements of this type — massive headline numbers tied to multi-year programs — are a known pattern that institutional desks tend to fade rather than chase; this is a structurally weak catalyst class for same-day strategies. Entering a stock already up 15% in five days with no stop meant the position was exposed to mean-reversion of the prior run with no defense beyond the scheduled exit.

executed.thesis: Spire Global signed an MoU with Schaeffler AG today (May 27) to develop space hardware subsystems and satellite platforms — a company-specific revenue-visibility catalyst in the satellite internet mainstreaming theme. Volume is 2.21x average and RSI at 67 is elevated but not extreme, suggesting the reaction is still developing rather than exhausted.
executed.outcome_notes: Stop triggered on a -3.5% reversal, indicating the elevated-volume pop faded and sellers reasserted within the session. An MoU is a letter of intent with no binding revenue commitment, which typically limits sustainable re-rating once the headline cycle exhausts.
executed.risks_observed: Soft catalysts (MoUs, partnership frameworks) are structurally prone to same-session fading once the initial print is digested — the elevated RSI at entry compounded this by leaving little room for further buyers. SPIR and AAL both shared the satellite internet theme and both hit stops on the same day, meaning thematic concentration across two concurrent positions amplified basket drawdown.

executed.thesis: American Airlines' confirmed Starlink deal for 500 narrowbody planes (announced May 26, still being absorbed at 1.79x volume) plus UBS Buy rating with $18 PT vs $14.85 close provides a 21% fundamental anchor. The satellite internet mainstreaming theme is the dominant sector narrative today, supporting continuation.
executed.outcome_notes: Stop triggered at -2.5%; selling pressure overwhelmed the volume-absorption thesis and the analyst price-target anchor provided no near-term floor. The catalyst was a May 26 announcement entered on May 27, meaning at least one full session of price discovery had already occurred before the position was opened.
executed.risks_observed: Day-old news creates a timing asymmetry — the sharpest continuation move typically occurs in the first session, leaving subsequent entries exposed to mean reversion rather than extension. Combined with SPIR sharing the same thematic narrative, the basket carried two correlated satellite-theme stops on a single day, a concentration risk that was not bounded at the portfolio level.

executed.thesis: IREN's $1.6B Blackwell hardware agreement with Dell published today adds fresh AI infrastructure revenue visibility in the session before tomorrow's earnings. The £-4.60 loss on zero price movement is purely transaction cost, flagging that the alpha window had likely closed before entry and the risk/reward was negative in expectation.

The thesis assumed two independent catalysts would compound, but if each was individually priced in by open, stacking them adds no incremental lift — a structural flaw for same-day multi-catalyst entries on large-caps.

executed.thesis: Cantor Fitzgerald raised PT to $416 today — a 27.6% implied upside from current levels — ahead of May 28 earnings where MongoDB's last reported surprise was +700%. Pre-earnings drift on strong analyst conviction with MACD histogram expanding positive (+3.53); 1-day hold exits before the earnings binary.

The analyst conviction signal failed to generate any intraday bid, suggesting the market either front-ran the upgrade earlier or was withholding commitment until the May 28 print itself.
executed.risks_observed: A single-day hold window gives drift almost no room to develop; the cost drag (spread + FX conversion) means even a small adverse tick books a net loss on a flat underlying. Pre-earnings drift trades are also vulnerable to the market flipping to 'wait-and-see' mode the closer the event gets, compressing the window further than the calendar implies.

executed.thesis: Breaking this morning: White House formally backing Intel's foundry buildout combined with reported potential supply agreements with Apple, NVIDIA, and SpaceX — a political/industrial policy catalyst that reframes INTC from struggling legacy chipmaker to strategic national asset. INTC's history of execution disappointments likely kept buyers cautious despite the policy tailwind, and a large-cap name absorbs headline flow without necessarily gapping.
executed.risks_observed: Policy catalysts for legacy industrials/semis carry a 'show me' discount — the market often requires evidence of contract signatures or budget line items before repricing, making the news-reaction window shorter and shallower than for pure momentum names. Both MDB and INTC being flat on the same day also points to a broader risk-off or low-conviction session that would have suppressed drift across the whole basket regardless of individual catalyst quality.

executed.thesis: AMD announced $10B+ Taiwan partnership commitment and 2nm EPYC Venice ramp for Helios Rack-Scale AI platforms today, delivering concrete AI capex evidence the day after Nvidia's beat validated the infrastructure spend cycle. The most likely mechanism was a classic coattail reversal: after Nvidia's beat the prior day, AMD latecomers were already long, the Taiwan partnership was treated as a cost commitment rather than a near-term revenue catalyst, and marginal buyers rotated back into Nvidia directly.
executed.risks_observed: Entering AMD as a second-order Nvidia beneficiary the day after Nvidia's blowout created asymmetric timing risk — the primary beneficiary had already absorbed the institutional flow, leaving AMD exposed to profit-taking with no independent catalyst strong enough to replace it. ARM and AMD held simultaneously produced semiconductor concentration; a sector-wide de-rating (which is what appears to have happened to AMD) risked both legs at once.

executed.thesis: Nvidia's earnings beat directly validates ARM's royalty revenue outlook as every data-center Nvidia chip runs on ARM IP; Bernstein $300 target (17% above current) and pre-market +3% continuation confirm institutional buyers are still accumulating into the agentic AI chip demand upgrade.

The royalty-leverage-to-AI-volumes thesis was the cleanest re-rating story of the four trades and attracted sustained buying through the session rather than a fade after the open. Scheduled exit captured the bulk of the single-day catalyst move.
executed.risks_observed: Entry followed a pre-market +3% move, meaning some of the catalyst was already priced and the position was exposed to a gap-fill reversal if NVDA's intraday action turned cautious. ARM's extreme P/E multiple means any softening of AI capex language — even in a different earnings call — compresses the multiple faster than it expanded; the upside captured here could unwind on a single macro headline.

executed.thesis: Raymond James upgrade to Outperform with $55 price target — 58% above current $34.81 — arrived yesterday with 2.26× volume and remains the freshest analyst catalyst in the energy sector; SM's recent debt paydown and +37.8% prior earnings beat provide fundamental support for the bullish re-rating.

Energy stocks are primarily driven by commodity price, not sell-side opinion, so the absence of a constructive oil tape left the upgrade catalyst structurally thin.
executed.risks_observed: A 58% gap between current price and the analyst target signals the upgrade originated from a deeply sceptical base rather than a momentum inflection, which limits buy-side credibility and urgency to act. Holding SM alongside three technology/pharma names meant this trade had no sector correlation hedge — if the broader basket was right-skewed on risk, SM's energy exposure added idiosyncratic downside with no offsetting relationship to the other positions.

executed.thesis: Cisco's May 13 Q3 earnings beat (paired with restructuring discipline in item 2.05) continues to attract buyers, and today's Rosenblatt $150 price target with 30% upside framing adds fresh institutional momentum to the one tech sub-sector (networking/AI infrastructure) holding up against bond-repricing headwinds. Volume is running at 1.28× the 20-day average today, confirming the market is still absorbing the news rather than already fully pricing it; Needham reiterates Buy at $120 (32% above current price), providing analyst-backed upside runway.
executed.outcome_notes: Price sold off through the stop rather than holding post-earnings support, indicating the initial gap or pop had already been absorbed before entry and there was no sustained follow-through from buyers. The double-beat catalyst failed to produce lasting demand, likely meaning the news was priced in on May 18 and the May 19 session represented distribution rather than continued accumulation.
executed.risks_observed: Entering a news-driven setup on the day after the 8-K filing rather than the same session exposed this trade to the common pattern of second-day fade once overnight momentum traders exit. Volume at 1.28× average was elevated but not conclusively strong, and sole reliance on a single analyst reiteration (rather than a wave of upgrades) left the upside case thin; no apparent catalyst to absorb selling pressure once the stop was tested.

executed.thesis: Publicis Groupe announced an all-cash acquisition of LiveRamp via a definitive merger agreement filed in an 8-K today (May 18); stock is trading at M&A arb discount to likely deal price (~$40) with 8x average volume confirming sustained institutional positioning in deal spread.

High volume confirmed institutional awareness of the spread, but that positioning was already reflected in the opening price, leaving no intraday compression to capture on a same-day exit.
executed.risks_observed: The thesis is structurally a multi-week arb, not an intraday catalyst play; a scheduled same-day exit is mismatched to the convergence timeline of a definitive merger agreement. Deal-break risk (regulatory, financing, competing bidder absence) is also unhedged, and any adverse headline would gap the stock well below entry with no stop in place.

executed.thesis: WSJ reported today that Elliott Management built a large activist stake in Bio-Rad; activist involvement is a strong and fresh catalyst for strategic action and multiple expansion, with RSI 55.8 leaving significant room before overbought conditions.

executed.risks_observed: Activist-stake disclosures can be front-run by prime brokerage desks before public reporting, so entry at open may already be late relative to the initial move. If the position is part of a basket with other activist-catalyst names, correlation spikes on broad risk-off days could compress the spread before strategic action materialises.

executed.thesis: BofA Securities reinstated ServiceNow as Buy with a $130 price target today (29% implied upside), stock is above both key moving averages with elevated relative volume of 0.65 suggesting institutional follow-through on the fresh analyst catalyst.

executed.risks_observed: Analyst reinstatements with wide price targets are frequently anticipated by sell-side desks ahead of publication, meaning a portion of the move may have already occurred before the open entry. With a scheduled exit and no stop, any intraday reversal — e.g., from a competing downgrade or sector sell-off — would have been held through in full.

executed.thesis: Benchmark raised Intel's price target to $140 today alongside Trump publicly signaling political support for Intel investment; after a -17.6% 5-day pullback from a massive +62% 20-day run, the stock has reset to a more favorable entry above both MAs.
executed.outcome_notes: The stock was flat on the session despite two fresh catalysts, with the price target raise from a secondary broker and political commentary failing to attract net buyers on the day. Post-run distribution pressure from the prior +62% move appears to have fully absorbed the catalyst flow.
executed.risks_observed: Entering after a parabolic 20-day run into a Benchmark (not tier-1) price target raise carries significant overhead supply risk; the thesis required momentum continuation but the prior move likely exhausted near-term buyers. Political signals are unreliable as price catalysts with no defined timeline, introducing further uncertainty about when or whether the thesis would resolve.

executed.thesis: NVIDIA initiated a 7.79M-share position in Coherent Corp (filed 2026-05-15), a direct institutional endorsement of COHR's role in AI optical networking infrastructure. RSI 63.3 is not overbought, volume is at-average (1.0x) rather than exhausted, suggesting the market is still absorbing the NVIDIA signal rather than having already fully priced it.

This position was also duplicated in the same session (see 4b7a7798), doubling COHR concentration on an identical signal without any new information.

VRT and COHR are both AI-infrastructure plays held simultaneously, adding sector-level correlation to the basket.

Running two full-size positions in COHR simultaneously inflated single-name concentration to levels that would have been painful had a sharp adverse move occurred.

A single adverse macro headline (rate spike, export-control news) could have hit both names simultaneously.

The macro catalysts cited (Currie call, Hormuz signal) are slow-moving and may not generate a single-session price move.

XOM provided sector diversification from the AI names but was the only energy position, leaving the strategy's non-AI leg thin.

active.description:
LLM-driven. Weights earnings surprises, M&A, guidance changes, and other
catalysts. News routing per ticker: Alpaca News for US-listed names,
yfinance fallback for UK/EU listings — coverage is decent everywhere.

executed.thesis: Fattal Hotel Group's formal $1.24bn takeover bid (announced 2026-05-29) is a confirmed M&A catalyst; today is the first full London trading session post-announcement and arbitrage capital entering should compress the remaining spread between current price and implied offer, with 4–6% intraday move plausible as institutional arb books open positions.
executed.outcome_notes: Price was completely flat from entry to the scheduled exit, meaning the expected arb spread compression never materialised intraday. The most likely explanation is that the spread had already closed in pre-market or in the prior session before London opened, leaving nothing to capture. The £-11.41 loss is pure transaction cost with no price contribution.
executed.risks_observed: M&A arb is acutely vulnerable to pre-open price discovery — by the time the first London print appeared, institutional arb desks may have already compressed the spread overnight. A scheduled-only exit with no stop meant the position had asymmetric downside if the deal had developed any uncertainty during the session. Single-name deal risk (bid withdrawal, regulatory hold) was live throughout with no hedge.

executed.thesis: ServiceNow's AI Control Tower announcement and multi-year enterprise partnerships with Experian and Wipro (May 30–31 news) catalysed a +14% single-session repricing; fresh news flow on top of existing momentum argues for intraday continuation as European markets open on the back of the US close strength.
executed.outcome_notes: The stop triggered at -4%, confirming that European hours did not continue the US session's strength — the stock reversed sharply from entry, consistent with profit-taking and 'buy the news, sell the continuation' dynamics after a +14% single-session move. The European listing lagged rather than echoed the US close, and the position was entered at the exhaustion point of the move rather than the beginning.
executed.risks_observed: Buying into a +14% single-session gap dramatically compresses the risk/reward: the entry was already pricing in the news, and any intraday fade hit the stop before any further upside could develop. Cross-venue momentum carries gap-and-fade risk specific to secondary listings where European price discovery reopens against an already-stretched US close. At the basket level, this trade and any other tech/AI-adjacent names on the same date would have been correlated to a broad European tech open, concentrating directional exposure.

executed.thesis: CVS today reinstated Zepbound as a co-preferred obesity drug — a direct PBM coverage catalyst that expands near-term script access and removes a meaningful headwind to GLP-1 revenue. Alongside positive Phase 1b Verve-102 data, the news flow is fresh and commercially concrete, unlike the long-dated R&D catalysts that have historically failed to reprice similar names intraday.
executed.outcome_notes: Take-profit triggered cleanly at +3%, consistent with a single concrete PBM catalyst repricing within a session — the CVS reinstatement news was commercially legible and the market reflected it without requiring multiple sessions to digest. Exit reason validates the thesis: this was a one-day access-expansion catalyst, not a multi-day re-rating.
executed.risks_observed: LLY.DE is part of a heavily traded GLP-1 theme where any negative Novo/VKTX headline intraday could have correlated the position adversely regardless of the Zepbound-specific catalyst. The basket on this day likely held both LLY and CVC, which are uncorrelated — but a broader risk-off move (macro print, geopolitical) could have swept both simultaneously.

executed.thesis: CVC's €4.65bn divestiture of its 13.8% Naturgy stake (announced May 27) is a capital-realization event the market is still digesting — stock is up +5.15% but RSI remains below 65 with normal volume. For a listed PE manager, a clean exit at scale supports the re-rating narrative and warrants a continuation trade while the catalyst is live.
executed.outcome_notes: The position captured only 1.1% before the scheduled close, suggesting the catalyst had largely been absorbed by the time of entry — the Naturgy announcement was two days old and the initial +5.15% move had already occurred. Price action was orderly but lacked the continuation momentum required for a stronger result.
executed.risks_observed: Entering on a two-day-old divestiture announcement with the stock already up over 5% introduced significant timing risk; without a fresh intraday trigger the edge was thin and dependent on slow institutional digestion rather than reactive repricing. No take-profit or trailing stop meant the position was fully exposed to mean-reversion if early buyers rotated out during the session.

executed.thesis: Barclays upgraded to Overweight with a doubled price target ($1,200→$2,300) while the company simultaneously crossed a profitability milestone and raised its dividend 20% — three fresh, concrete catalysts arriving together signal institutional re-rating is still early; AI-era multiyear NAND supply agreements add duration to the thesis beyond today's news cycle.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly in the direction of the catalyst, adding over 5% before the scheduled close — the multi-catalyst setup (upgrade + profitability + dividend) sustained buying pressure across the session rather than fading after the open. The scheduled exit left gains on the table if momentum continued after close, but the thesis held intraday without reversal.
executed.risks_observed: A scheduled exit with no trailing stop means the position had no downside protection if the upgrade repricing had been front-run or faded post-open; the 5% move suggests it wasn't, but the structure was blind to that risk. WDC.DE as a German-listed wrapper adds FX and liquidity spread risk not present in the US-listed underlying, particularly relevant on a high-vol catalyst day.

executed.thesis: Lufthansa's executive directly confirmed 'Summer's Good to Go' — stable fuel supply and visible summer booking demand supporting the full-year earnings outlook, a specific management guidance event not yet fully priced; new supervisory board chair appointment simultaneously removes a governance uncertainty that had been an overhang.
executed.outcome_notes: The scheduled exit rather than take_profit indicates the management guidance event repriced the stock only partially — price drifted in the right direction but lacked the follow-through momentum to hit target within the holding window. The governance catalyst (board chair change) appears to have contributed little incremental lift; the gain reflects the booking-demand headline being digested slowly rather than sharply.
executed.risks_observed: Soft-catalyst trades like a verbal management reassurance carry high sensitivity to how much the market had already discounted the message — this outcome is consistent with the 'good to go' framing being largely expected. Combined with the AIR.DE position, the session carried concentrated European aviation exposure with no hedge against a demand-side shock or fuel-cost news that could have turned both trades simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Dual fresh catalyst: Airbus positioned as Canada helicopter export hub for NATO defense spending (ongoing re-rating theme), and American Airlines Starlink deal deployed across 500+ Airbus jets signals durable fleet demand. Last earnings surprise +35.6%, RSI 52 with room to run, and 0.30% round-trip cost clears the bar cleanly.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly to the take_profit level, confirming the market was actively repricing the defense-spend re-rating narrative rather than fading it intraday. The orderly exit with no apparent reversal attempt suggests institutional buying absorbed the catalyst without exhaustion — the Starlink fleet-demand angle likely broadened the buyer base beyond pure defense allocators.
executed.risks_observed: Both catalysts are thematic re-ratings rather than hard data points, meaning any reversal in NATO spending headlines or a broader aerospace sell-off could have unwound the position before the target was reached. Running this alongside LHA.DE on the same session added correlated EUR-denominated aviation exposure — a single macro shock (e.g. a fuel spike or Eurozone risk-off) would have hit both legs simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Today's investor-day announcement of AI consulting mid-term targets is a genuine same-session catalyst; Capgemini is repositioning as an enterprise AI implementation consultant, which should attract re-rating buying as the market prices in the growth runway. MACD histogram turning positive confirms emerging momentum.
executed.outcome_notes: The investor-day catalyst produced zero same-session price movement — entry and exit prices were identical, with the £-17.80 loss attributable entirely to spread and EUR/GBP conversion drag. The anticipated re-rating buying never arrived within the holding window; the scheduled exit simply closed a dead position rather than capturing any directional move.
executed.risks_observed: Flat price action on an investor-day event strongly suggests the market had pre-positioned or that the AI consulting targets were already consensus — a recurring risk for news-reactive entries where institutional flow precedes the public announcement. EUR-listed names carry a structural FX cost on GBP-denominated books that meaningfully erodes any thin edge, and MACD confirmation on a news-day entry can reflect pre-event drift rather than genuine post-announcement momentum.

executed.thesis: Trump administration's $1 billion quantum foundry grant to IBM, announced today (2026-05-22), is a fresh hard-dollar government catalyst with immediate repricing implications. Volume at 2.37× the 20-day average confirms institutional buying is already underway; 1-day hold captures the event-day move before the news is fully digested.
executed.outcome_notes: The quantum grant failed to produce sustained intraday repricing — price sold off from entry through the scheduled exit, suggesting the catalyst was either front-run before the open or dismissed as a long-dated, non-revenue event. Volume confirmation at entry did not persist into buying pressure; the 2.37× spike likely reflected opening-auction noise rather than durable institutional accumulation.
executed.risks_observed: Government R&D grants carry optionality-style value that markets often discount steeply on day one, making them poor 1-day catalysts relative to revenue or earnings surprises. IBM.DE as a German-listed wrapper adds intraday EUR/USD drag that compounds against a falling underlying. No intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed rather than cut when the thesis failed to materialize within the first hour.

executed.thesis: Phase 3 retatrutide data showing up to 28.3% weight loss over 80 weeks is a major pipeline upgrade for Eli Lilly's obesity franchise; the low cost gate (0.30%) gives ample margin versus the expected move, and healthcare is insulated from today's central-bank and China macro headwinds.
executed.outcome_notes: Price moved in the expected direction and held through the scheduled exit, consistent with the Phase 3 readout being a genuine pipeline upgrade rather than a pre-leaked or already-priced event. The healthcare sector's macro insulation held on the day, removing a common headwind that affected other sectors.
executed.risks_observed: Phase 3 weight-loss data carries binary read-through risk — a miss or safety signal would have produced a sharp reversal well beyond the 0.30% cost gate, and a scheduled exit offers no protection in that scenario. Both legs of today's basket are German-listed wrappers of US-domiciled names, meaning correlated EUR/USD exposure sits unhedged across the book; on a day with USD strength, that drag would have clipped both positions simultaneously.

executed.thesis: Rheinmetall's Q1 2026 earnings beat (sales €1,938m vs prior-year €1,800m, net income up) continues to drive institutional re-rating with RSI at 39.7 well below overbought levels; NATO spending tailwinds provide structural support for a 2-day post-results drift continuation below both key moving averages.
executed.outcome_notes: T212 paper portfolio was reset on 2026-06-01 (platform-level reset by user). Position was force-cleared in the ledger because the broker-side state was wiped; no real fill price was captured. Treat P&L as missing for evaluation.
executed.risks_observed: Real fill price not captured because the platform reset preceded the close.

executed.thesis: RS Group reported full-year FY2026 earnings today with a 3.41x volume surge, the clearest signal of institutional accumulation on results day. Strong cash flow generation and the 'building momentum' narrative gives the market permission to re-rate; today's session is the primary catalyst window before the story is fully digested.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted lower through the session and never reclaimed entry, closing out on the scheduled exit with no recovery attempt. The volume surge on results day appears to have marked distribution rather than accumulation — institutional buyers did not follow through into the close, and the 'building momentum' narrative failed to generate same-day price continuation.
executed.risks_observed: No intraday stop meant the full drawdown was absorbed passively; a trailing stop or time-based cut would have reduced the loss. Earnings-day volume spikes are ambiguous signals — they can represent two-way institutional activity rather than directional conviction. Entering on results day creates binary exposure: if the move is already priced by open, there is limited upside and a full session of potential mean-reversion.

executed.thesis: Currys upgraded FY profit guidance on May 19 with LFL sales +4%, and last earnings surprise was +59.4% — a pattern of consistent beats that analysts will be forced to model. RSI 64.7 leaves room before overbought, and sell-side target price revisions typically arrive the day after a retail profit upgrade, extending the move into Day 2.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted cleanly from 1.44 to 1.47, consistent with continued post-upgrade momentum rather than a sharp catalyst spike. The exit was scheduled rather than signal-driven, so it's ambiguous whether the anticipated analyst target-price revision actually arrived intraday or whether the move was simply residual buying from the May 19 announcement. No reversal before exit — the directional call held.
executed.risks_observed: Scheduled exit severs any feedback loop on whether the analyst revision catalyst materialised, making it hard to distinguish thesis validation from coincidental drift. A time-based exit also leaves upside on the table if the revision cycle extended into Day 2 or Day 3 as originally hypothesised. At the basket level, a single UK consumer-discretionary name with no paired short means any broad retail sector reversal — e.g., a weak consumer confidence print — carried unhedged downside.

executed.thesis: Corvex Management's public call for a Whitbread sale (May 18) establishes a live M&A premium — activist campaigns of this type typically sustain elevated pricing as long as no deal is rejected. Stock remains above both SMAs with RSI 54.7, and the story is likely to receive additional press coverage today, supporting a continued bid.
executed.outcome_notes: The stock edged slightly higher as expected, but the gross gain was insufficient to clear transaction costs, producing a net loss despite correct directional call. The absence of a meaningful intraday move suggests the Corvex catalyst had already been substantially absorbed in the days prior to entry.
executed.risks_observed: Activist M&A campaigns re-rate quickly on initial press; entering three days after the Corvex announcement likely meant buying into an already-priced premium with little incremental catalyst remaining for the session. Holding two news-driven trades simultaneously (earnings + M&A) on the same day concentrates the book around the shared 'catalyst already digested' failure mode — both positions essentially faced the same risk that the news was stale by entry.

executed.thesis: Q1 earnings beat (sales €1.94B vs €1.80B, net income up) combined with today's fresh institutional analysis coverage keeps the reaction developing; RSI at 38.8 after a 20-day correction leaves substantial room before overbought conditions, and the FX-only cost structure (0.30% round-trip) gives favourable risk/reward versus LSE names.

executed.thesis: Fresh Strait of Hormuz crisis coverage (2026-05-17) plus a new Eastern Mediterranean deep-offshore gas MOU with Egypt give TotalEnergies a dual catalyst — supply disruption premium and strategic gas expansion — that has not yet fully lifted volume off its below-average base, leaving room for catch-up.

Below-average volume at entry, flagged as a potential catch-up signal, instead indicated lack of conviction; the catalysts may have been too diffuse or already partially priced into the energy complex broadly.

active.description:
Long-short sector pair strategy on GBP-denominated LSE-listed ETFs.
Picks one long sector ETF (the strongest cross-sectional momentum) +
one inverse / hedge ETF position to neutralise market beta. The
trade extracts the cross-sectional sector spread rather than market
direction, which means it should produce return that's structurally
uncorrelated with the rest of the slate (all of which are
long-only and fully market-exposed when deployed).

Axis broken: EXPOSURE. Everything else in the slate runs long-only
with +1.0 market beta when fully invested; this strategy targets
net market beta near zero. Even if its standalone Sharpe is modest,
its low correlation with the rest of the slate is what makes it
valuable to the tournament — distinguishability on the leaderboard.

Universe is eu_etfs_sector + selected inverse / hedge ETFs from
eu_etfs_bond and eu_etfs_commodity (gold, gilts) so the LLM can
pick a true hedge when no inverse-sector ETF matches the laggard
sector cleanly.

executed.thesis: Euro Stoxx IT is the strongest EU-listed name in the universe with +19.51% 20d momentum, and today's 2.06x volume surge confirms institutional conviction entering June. Pair 1 long leg: captures the EU tech catch-up trade with ECB easing as an independent rate tailwind; hedge leg unavailable in universe so 55% cash acts as the implicit offset, keeping portfolio beta ≈ 0.40.

Pair 2 long leg on a distinct macro theme: dollar weakness (DXY -0.28% week) directly lifts USD-denominated materials, and XSMW's MACD histogram at +0.106 shows the sharpest momentum acceleration outside tech. Diversifies the portfolio away from the AI/rate-cut narrative into the FX/commodity cycle.
executed.outcome_notes: Price went nowhere — entry and exit were identical, suggesting the dollar-weakness/materials thesis never catalysed any move during the holding period. The scheduled exit rather than a stop or target hit indicates the trade was simply timed out without the macro driver materialising into price action.
executed.risks_observed: A flat exit on a momentum-driven thesis points to the MACD signal being noise rather than a leading indicator on this name; histogram readings this small are easily overwhelmed by spread and slippage, which is likely what the £-12 loss represents. At basket level, anchoring a diversification leg to a single macro factor (DXY) with no catalyst timing creates dead-weight exposure when the FX move stalls intraday.

active.description:
Calendar-triggered, axis-breaking variant. Trades stocks that have
just reported earnings, going long on confirmed beat-and-raise prints
and avoiding the rest. Post-earnings announcement drift (Bernard &
Thomas 1989; replicated for ~40 years) is the most-replicated cross-
sectional anomaly in equity markets: beats drift up for ~60 days,
misses drift down. This sleeve harvests the long side.

Distinct from the rest of the slate in TRIGGER (earnings calendar,
not periodic rebalance) and TIME-SLICE (entries cluster around
earnings windows, dormant between). Hold target 15-25 trading days
to capture the drift without overlapping the next quarter's
announcement.

active.description:
LLM-driven. Trades sector ETFs based on relative momentum and macro
alignment. US: SPDR sector ETFs (XLF, XLE, XLK, ...). UK/EU: GBP-
denominated iShares MSCI Europe sector ETFs (ESIF.L, ESIT.L, ...) —
GBP avoids the FX fee the older EUR STOXX-600 lines carried. Same
strategy bias, different ETF universe per region.

executed.thesis: Semiconductor ETF with 20d +30.15% and 5d +10.66% is the cleanest expression of the dominant tech/AI revival macro thesis — above both SMAs, RSI 72.8 confirms strong momentum without the extreme extension of RAYS.L (78.2), and the oil-collapse yield decline provides direct DCF tailwind for the sector. Predicted 3.5% over 2 days clears the 3.0% cost gate.
executed.outcome_notes: T212 paper portfolio was reset on 2026-06-01 (platform-level reset by user). Position was force-cleared in the ledger because the broker-side state was wiped; no real fill price was captured. Treat P&L as missing for evaluation.
executed.risks_observed: Real fill price not captured because the platform reset preceded the close.

executed.thesis: Defense ETF with the strongest volume confirmation in the entire candidate set (1.67× avg) signaling institutional accumulation, dual-timeframe momentum leadership (+12.50% 5d / +17.66% 20d), and a structural defense-spending tailwind that is independent of the oil/yield regime flip.
executed.outcome_notes: Price declined steadily from entry to exit with no recovery, suggesting the institutional accumulation signal was either a false read or the position was entered too late in the momentum cycle. The scheduled exit enforced discipline but the trade never developed any positive follow-through, indicating the defense tailwind thesis did not translate into near-term price support during the holding period.
executed.risks_observed: Volume confirmation alone proved insufficient as a momentum signal — high volume can mark distribution as readily as accumulation. The ETF structure adds a layer of tracking/liquidity spread risk that can erode edge on shorter holding periods, and no intraday stop was in place to cut the loss before the scheduled exit.

executed.thesis: Strongest 5d performer in the universe (+18.58%) with a fresh bullish MACD crossover (line above signal) and RSI only 57.8 — unusually unextended for a leveraged product this strong, suggesting the momentum phase has more room before exhaustion; wider stops set at ~1 ATR for the leveraged instrument.
executed.outcome_notes: A 17-point drawdown on a leveraged product held to a scheduled exit indicates the underlying index reversed sharply after entry, overwhelming the MACD crossover signal entirely. The RSI headroom thesis failed because leveraged ETFs can compress violently on any mean-reversion in the underlying, regardless of how unextended the initial reading appeared.
executed.risks_observed: Leveraged instruments carry path-dependency and daily-reset decay that make multi-day holds structurally hostile even when the directional call is roughly correct; the ~1 ATR stop was too wide for a 3× product where a 6% underlying move produces an 18% instrument loss. Holding this alongside DFNX.L created correlated European-market exposure that compounded drawdown when the session turned risk-off across the basket.

executed.thesis: European Banks are the strongest consistent 20d relative-strength leader (+2.41% vs broad EU benchmark) with MACD accelerating positively, RSI 65.2 (momentum intact but not extended), and a credit backdrop described as 'benign and slightly improving' in the macro view. Yield curve at 97bp NIM tailwind and ECB policy hold support the sector bid.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted steadily higher from entry and closed near the session high, consistent with continued institutional rotation into EU financials on the ECB hold narrative. The scheduled exit captured the full intraday move but was time-driven, not signal-driven — no evidence the thesis broke down before close.
executed.risks_observed: A scheduled exit provides no dynamic protection if the move reverses late in the session; a trailing stop would have defended more of the gain had price given back ground. Single-sector concentration in EU banks means any intraday ECB commentary or credit-spread widening could gap the ETF against the position with no mitigation visible in this trade's structure.

executed.thesis: European Banks hold the highest 20d relative strength of any candidate (+2.41% vs Euro benchmark), with a constructive 97bp yield curve maintaining NIM support; price sits cleanly above both SMAs with a positive MACD trend, making this the clearest second-sector beneficiary of the transitional macro pivot away from pure stagflation.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted modestly higher from entry to exit, consistent with the relative-strength thesis holding but without conviction — the 16bp gain over a scheduled hold suggests the sector simply tracked the broader market rather than outperforming on any discrete catalyst. Exit was time-driven, not signal-driven, so no information about thesis exhaustion is captured here.
executed.risks_observed: A scheduled exit with no stop means the position had uncapped downside during the hold period; had European bank sentiment reversed intraday on ECB commentary or credit spread widening, the strategy had no automatic exit mechanism. Single-sector concentration in financials also means any correlated drawdown across the basket on a risk-off day would have been amplified with no offsetting hedge.

executed.thesis: EXV3.DE is the unambiguous sector leader: 5d +4.18% / 20d +8.77%, a 3.29x volume surge confirming institutional participation, RSI 66.9 (strong momentum, not yet extended), and the energy supply-shock macro regime showing no reversal signal. Two consecutive winning sessions validate the continuation setup; a 2-day hold captures the sector rotation move while wider stops accommodate ETF-level noise.

Strongest candidate by both 5d (+1.79%) and 20d (+6.28%) relative strength, above rising SMA20 and SMA50, RSI 62.5 not overbought. The macro energy supply-shock thesis (USO elevated, XLE ranked #1 sector) provides direct tailwind with no reversal signal — yesterday's +0.47% was a low-volume day and the trend structure is intact heading into day 2.
executed.outcome_notes: Trade closed at schedule with a clean 2.35% gain, confirming the trend continuation thesis. Price action followed through on the energy supply-shock tailwind without needing the stop as a backstop — the scheduled exit captured the move without overstaying.
executed.risks_observed: Single-sector concentration in energy means the gain is tightly correlated with USO/XLE sentiment; a reversal in crude overnight would have unwound this quickly. No trailing stop meant the full position was exposed to any intraday spike-and-reverse that happened to close near entry.

executed.thesis: Second-best performer in the candidate set (5d +2.38%, 20d +4.12%), above both SMAs, consistent with the mildly bullish XLV healthcare view as a defensive rotation leg. The 5d and 20d momentum that justified the entry did not translate into day-of follow-through, suggesting relative strength was already fading at entry.

The tighter stop intended to limit downside was not tight enough to avoid the loss, indicating the stop sizing may not be calibrated to recent EXH1.DE volatility.

With no intraday stop on the position, a sharp energy reversal after entry would have had no circuit-breaker.

executed.thesis: Consumer Staples (Food & Beverage) leads the candidate set on 5d returns (+3.90%) and is the defensive rotation trade aligned with the macro stagflationary backdrop; above both MAs with a positive MACD, it rounds out a concentrated Energy + Defensives portfolio that avoids every macro-bearish sector.

The scheduled exit prevented further drawdown but offered no active management of the deteriorating tape.
executed.risks_observed: The basket ran three positions with only one net winner, and the two losers were in adjacent defensive sub-sectors that moved in lockstep — the portfolio's effective sector diversification was lower than the ticker count implied. Momentum-at-entry as the primary signal carries look-back bias risk; a single strong 5d window can reflect an already-exhausted move rather than an ongoing one.

executed.thesis: EXH1.DE (European Oil & Gas) is the clearest regime trade: best 5d (+1.9%) and 20d (+5.6%) relative strength in the candidate set, above both SMA20 and SMA50, with the macro thesis fully aligned — the oil supply shock makes energy the highest-conviction sector rotation this week. Slightly tighter stop given established trend, wider take profit to capture the oil momentum leg.
executed.outcome_notes: Price drifted in the right direction but the oil momentum leg never accelerated — a scheduled exit rather than a take-profit hit signals the supply-shock catalyst was either already priced or failed to reprice within the holding window. The above-SMA positioning held and the trade closed green, but the move was consistent with noise rather than a regime trend.
executed.risks_observed: Single-sector energy concentration meant any intraday reversal in oil sentiment (OPEC commentary, demand revision) would have flipped this to a loss with minimal warning. The asymmetry of a tighter stop against a wider take-profit was not rewarded here, and the scheduled exit left potential upside on the table had momentum arrived later in the session.

executed.thesis: EXV3.DE (European Technology) is flagging a breakout: volume 3.69x the 20-day average is the strongest flow signal in the set today, price is above both SMAs, RSI at 61 with positive MACD histogram confirms the setup; the AI capex cycle remains intact per the macro view, making this a technically-confirmed entry into the second-ranked macro sector.
executed.outcome_notes: The volume spike did not produce price follow-through — exit below entry on a scheduled close suggests the 3.69x volume bar was more likely absorption or distribution than genuine accumulation, invalidating the breakout read at entry. RSI and MACD confirmed momentum at the time but were lagging the actual flow dynamic.
executed.risks_observed: Elevated volume without same-session price confirmation is a known false-breakout pattern; the signal weighting should distinguish between demand-driven and supply-driven volume spikes. Running this alongside EXH1.DE created a two-leg basket where a broad risk-off move would have hit both simultaneously, and with neither stop triggered on the day, full notional was exposed throughout — no safety net fired.

executed.thesis: European Energy ETF aligned with the top-ranked macro theme — oil +27.7% 20d, sector +7.15% 20d, holding above both SMA20 and SMA50 with RSI 60 (momentum without being overbought); the mild 5d pullback (-0.10%) into MACD support is a clean entry within an intact uptrend.

The scheduled exit prevented any capture of the momentum the thesis anticipated, suggesting the holding period was too short relative to the macro driver's cycle. No information was generated about whether the MACD support level was meaningful.
executed.risks_observed: Energy ETFs carry sharp reversal risk if oil momentum stalls or geopolitical supply narrative shifts intraday — a flat exit masks the fact that no stop was tested, not that no risk existed. Single-commodity-linked sector concentration means correlation to oil swings is essentially unhedged at the basket level, and both positions here share European-listed exposure, compounding EUR FX drag risk.
